13	# ColorPicker
14	
15	A `ColorPicker` lets the user select a color through a combination of a 2D area (saturation
16	and lightness), a hue channel strip, an optional alpha channel strip, and optional text
17	inputs for individual channels. It supports multiple color formats (HSL, HSB, RGB, HEX)
18	and includes an optional EyeDropper browser API integration.
19	
20	## Color Contrast Responsibility
21	
22	`ColorPicker` is a **data entry component**; contrast validation of the selected color is the **application's responsibility**, not the component's. The component provides a color selection UI — it does not (and cannot) know how the selected color will be used (background, text, border, etc.).
23	
24	- Adapters MAY provide an optional **contrast checker widget** (e.g., a badge showing the WCAG contrast ratio against a reference color) as a composable companion component, but this is NOT part of the core `ColorPicker` machine.
25	- Applications that use `ColorPicker` for theme building or text color selection SHOULD validate the selected color against WCAG 2.1 contrast requirements: **4.5:1** minimum for normal text, **3:1** for large text (>=18pt or >=14pt bold).
26	- The `ColorValue` type exposes a `relative_luminance() -> f64` method that can be used for contrast ratio calculation: `contrast_ratio = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)` where `L1` is the lighter luminance.
27	
28	## Types
29	
30	The internal color representation is `ColorValue` (HSL + alpha). All other spaces are
31	computed on demand via conversion methods on `ColorValue`.
32	
33	```rust,no_check
34	// crates/ars-core/src/color.rs
35	//
36	// The shared color value types live in `ars-core` (flat `color` module,
37	// re-exported at the crate root) so every color component — ColorSwatch,
38	// ColorField, ColorArea, ColorSlider, ColorWheel, ColorSwatchPicker, and
39	// ColorPicker — consumes them as `ars_core::color::{ColorValue, ColorChannel, …}`.
40	
41	/// A color value stored in HSL with alpha. All other formats are computed.
42	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
43	pub struct ColorValue {
44	    /// Hue in degrees [0, 360).
45	    pub hue: f64,
46	    /// Saturation as a fraction [0.0, 1.0].
47	    pub saturation: f64,
48	    /// Lightness as a fraction [0.0, 1.0].
49	    pub lightness: f64,
50	    /// Alpha as a fraction [0.0, 1.0].
51	    pub alpha: f64,
52	}
53	
54	impl ColorValue {
55	    /// Create a new `ColorValue` from the given hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha.
56	    ///
57	    /// Hue is wrapped into `[0, 360)`; saturation, lightness, and alpha are
58	    /// clamped to `[0.0, 1.0]`. Non-finite inputs (`NaN`/`inf`) are coerced to
59	    /// `0.0` so the result is always a valid color.
60	    pub fn new(hue: f64, saturation: f64, lightness: f64, alpha: f64) -> Self {
61	        // Coerce non-finite inputs to `0.0` so the type's invariants (finite
62	        // components, hue in `[0, 360)`, others in `[0, 1]`) hold in release
63	        // builds too — otherwise `NaN`/`inf` would leak into generated CSS and
64	        // ARIA. Parsers already reject non-finite user input; this guards the
65	        // public constructor against programmatic non-finite values.
66	        let finite = |value: f64| if value.is_finite() { value } else { 0.0 };
67	        Self {
68	            hue: finite(hue).rem_euclid(360.0),
69	            saturation: finite(saturation).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
70	            lightness: finite(lightness).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
71	            alpha: finite(alpha).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
72	        }
73	    }
74	
75	    /// Create from an HSL triplet with full alpha.
76	    pub fn from_hsl(h: f64, s: f64, l: f64) -> Self {
77	        Self::new(h, s, l, 1.0)
78	    }
79	
80	    /// Convert to RGB (0-255 per channel).
81	    pub fn to_rgb(&self) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
82	        let h = self.hue / 360.0;
83	        let s = self.saturation;
84	        let l = self.lightness;
85	        let c = (1.0 - (2.0 * l - 1.0).abs()) * s;
86	        let x = c * (1.0 - ((h * 6.0) % 2.0 - 1.0).abs());
87	        let m = l - c / 2.0;
88	        let (r1, g1, b1) = match (h * 6.0).floor() as u8 {
89	            0 => (c, x, 0.0),
90	            1 => (x, c, 0.0),
91	            2 => (0.0, c, x),
92	            3 => (0.0, x, c),
93	            4 => (x, 0.0, c),
94	            _ => (c, 0.0, x),
95	        };
96	        (
97	            ((r1 + m) * 255.0).round() as u8,
98	            ((g1 + m) * 255.0).round() as u8,
99	            ((b1 + m) * 255.0).round() as u8,
100	        )
101	    }
102	
103	    /// Convert to RGBA (0-255 per channel, alpha 0-255).
104	    pub fn to_rgba(&self) -> (u8, u8, u8, u8) {
105	        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();
106	        (r, g, b, (self.alpha * 255.0).round() as u8)
107	    }
108	
109	    /// Convert to hex string (6-digit or 8-digit with alpha).
110	    pub fn to_hex(&self, include_alpha: bool) -> String {
111	        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();
112	        if include_alpha && self.alpha < 1.0 {
113	            let a = (self.alpha * 255.0).round() as u8;
114	            format!("#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}", r, g, b, a)
115	        } else {
116	            format!("#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}", r, g, b)
117	        }
118	    }
119	
120	    /// Convert to CSS hsl() or hsla() string.
121	    pub fn to_css_hsl(&self) -> String {
122	        if self.alpha < 1.0 {
123	            format!(
124	                "hsla({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%, {:.2})",
125	                self.hue,
126	                self.saturation * 100.0,
127	                self.lightness * 100.0,
128	                self.alpha,
129	            )
130	        } else {
131	            format!(
132	                "hsl({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)",
133	                self.hue,
134	                self.saturation * 100.0,
135	                self.lightness * 100.0,
136	            )
137	        }
138	    }
139	
140	    /// Convert to HSB/HSV representation.
141	    pub fn to_hsb(&self) -> (f64, f64, f64) {
142	        let l = self.lightness;
143	        let s = self.saturation;
144	        let v = l + s * l.min(1.0 - l);
145	        let sv = if v == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { 2.0 * (1.0 - l / v) };
146	        (self.hue, sv, v)
147	    }
148	
149	    /// Create from RGB values (0-255).
150	    pub fn from_rgb(r: u8, g: u8, b: u8) -> Self {
151	        let r = r as f64 / 255.0;
152	        let g = g as f64 / 255.0;
153	        let b = b as f64 / 255.0;
154	        let max = r.max(g).max(b);
155	        let min = r.min(g).min(b);
156	        let l = (max + min) / 2.0;
157	        if max == min {
158	            return Self::new(0.0, 0.0, l, 1.0);
159	        }
160	        let d = max - min;
161	        let s = if l > 0.5 { d / (2.0 - max - min) } else { d / (max + min) };
162	        let h = if max == r {
163	            ((g - b) / d + if g < b { 6.0 } else { 0.0 }) * 60.0
164	        } else if max == g {
165	            ((b - r) / d + 2.0) * 60.0
166	        } else {
167	            ((r - g) / d + 4.0) * 60.0
168	        };
169	        Self::new(h, s, l, 1.0)
170	    }
171	
172	    /// Parse a hex string ("#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa").
173	    pub fn from_hex(hex: &str) -> Option<Self> {
174	        // Strip at most one leading `#`. `trim_start_matches` would swallow
175	        // extra markers, accepting malformed input like `##3366ff`.
176	        let hex = hex.strip_prefix('#').unwrap_or(hex);
177	
178	        // Hex digits are ASCII. Reject non-ASCII early so the byte-indexed
179	        // slices below cannot land on a non-char boundary and panic (a
180	        // multi-byte string such as `ああ` is exactly 6 bytes).
181	        if !hex.is_ascii() {
182	            return None;
183	        }
184	
185	        match hex.len() {
186	            6 => {
187	                let r = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[0..2], 16).ok()?;
188	                let g = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[2..4], 16).ok()?;
189	                let b = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[4..6], 16).ok()?;
190	                Some(Self::from_rgb(r, g, b))
191	            }
192	            8 => {
193	                let r = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[0..2], 16).ok()?;
194	                let g = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[2..4], 16).ok()?;
195	                let b = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[4..6], 16).ok()?;
196	                let a = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[6..8], 16).ok()?;
197	                let mut color = Self::from_rgb(r, g, b);
198	                color.alpha = a as f64 / 255.0;
199	                Some(color)
200	            }
201	            _ => None,
202	        }
203	    }
204	}
205	
206	impl Default for ColorValue {
207	    fn default() -> Self {
208	        Self::new(0.0, 1.0, 0.5, 1.0) // Pure red, full opacity
209	    }
210	}

212	
213	### Contrast Ratio Utility Functions
214	
215	To assist applications that use `ColorPicker` for theme building or accessible color selection, the following utility functions are provided on `ColorValue`:
216	
217	```rust
218	impl ColorValue {
219	    /// Compute the relative luminance per WCAG 2.1 definition.
220	    /// Uses the sRGB linearization formula: if C <= 0.04045, C/12.92;
221	    /// else ((C + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4. Returns a value in [0.0, 1.0].
222	    pub fn relative_luminance(&self) -> f64 {
223	        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();
224	        fn linearize(c: u8) -> f64 {
225	            let c = c as f64 / 255.0;
226	            if c <= 0.04045 { c / 12.92 } else { ((c + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4) }
227	        }
228	        0.2126 * linearize(r) + 0.7152 * linearize(g) + 0.0722 * linearize(b)
229	    }
230	
231	    /// Compute the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two colors.
232	    /// Returns a value in [1.0, 21.0]. Higher is more contrast.
233	    pub fn contrast_ratio(&self, other: &ColorValue) -> f64 {
234	        let l1 = self.relative_luminance();
235	        let l2 = other.relative_luminance();
236	        let (lighter, darker) = if l1 > l2 { (l1, l2) } else { (l2, l1) };
237	        (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)
238	    }
239	
240	    /// Check if this color passes WCAG AA contrast against another color.
241	    /// Normal text: 4.5:1; large text (>= 18pt or >= 14pt bold): 3:1.
242	    pub fn passes_wcag_aa(&self, other: &ColorValue, large_text: bool) -> bool {
243	        let ratio = self.contrast_ratio(other);
244	        if large_text { ratio >= 3.0 } else { ratio >= 4.5 }
245	    }
246	
247	    /// Check if this color passes WCAG AAA contrast against another color.
248	    /// Normal text: 7:1; large text: 4.5:1.
249	    pub fn passes_wcag_aaa(&self, other: &ColorValue, large_text: bool) -> bool {
250	        let ratio = self.contrast_ratio(other);
251	        if large_text { ratio >= 4.5 } else { ratio >= 7.0 }
252	    }
253	}
254	```
255	
256	**Usage example** (application-level validation):
257	
258	```rust,no_check
259	let foreground = color_picker_api.value();
260	let background = ColorValue::from_hex("#ffffff").unwrap();
261	let ratio = foreground.contrast_ratio(&background);
262	let passes = foreground.passes_wcag_aa(&background, false);
263	// Display: "Contrast ratio: 4.7:1 AA" or "2.1:1 Fails AA"
264	```
265	
266	These utilities are provided as helpers on `ColorValue` in `ars-core`. The component itself does not validate or enforce contrast -- this remains the application's responsibility.
267	
268	### Color Name Parts
269	
270	```rust
271	/// Describes a color in human-readable terms for screen readers.
272	/// Components: lightness modifier, chroma modifier, and hue name.
273	/// Parts are returned as `String` (not `&'static str`) to support localized labels.
274	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
275	pub struct ColorNameParts {
276	    /// e.g., "dark", "light", "very dark", "very light", or "" for medium.
277	    pub lightness: String,
278	    /// e.g., "vibrant", "pale", "grayish", or "" for moderate.
279	    pub chroma: String,
280	    /// e.g., "red", "blue", "cyan-blue", "gray", "white", "black".
281	    pub hue: String,
282	}
283	
284	impl ColorValue {
285	    /// Returns English color-description parts for accessibility.
286	    ///
287	    /// The parts are English keys (e.g. lightness `"dark"`, chroma `"vibrant"`,
288	    /// hue `"blue"`); a component's `format_name` message maps and reorders them
289	    /// per locale (English: `"{lightness} {chroma} {hue}"`, Italian:
290	    /// `"{hue} {chroma} {lightness}"`). Keeping the keys English here decouples
291	    /// `ColorValue` from any single component's `Messages`.
292	    ///
293	    /// Classification runs in OKLCH (perceptually uniform):
294	    /// 1. Convert HSL -> sRGB -> OKLab -> OKLCH (Björn Ottosson's transform).
295	    /// 2. Lightness -> 5 levels: very dark (0-0.2), dark (0.2-0.4),
296	    ///    medium/`""` (0.4-0.6), light (0.6-0.8), very light (>=0.8).
297	    /// 3. Chroma: grayish (<0.04), moderate/`""` (0.04-0.12), vibrant (>0.12).
298	    ///    Moderate chroma with light lightness reads as "pale".
299	    /// 4. Hue angle -> 13 named hues: red, red-orange, orange, yellow-orange,
300	    ///    yellow, yellow-green, green, cyan-green, cyan, cyan-blue, blue,
301	    ///    purple, magenta.
302	    /// 5. Near-zero chroma collapses to "gray"/"white"/"black" by lightness.
303	    pub fn color_name_parts(&self) -> ColorNameParts {
304	        let (lightness, chroma, hue) = self.oklch_classify();
305	        ColorNameParts {
306	            lightness: lightness.to_string(),
307	            chroma: chroma.to_string(),
308	            hue: hue.to_string(),
309	        }
310	    }
311	
312	    /// Convenience: format as an English-order string such as "dark vibrant blue".
313	    /// Joins the non-empty parts with single spaces.
314	    pub fn color_name_en(&self) -> String {
315	        let parts = self.color_name_parts();
316	        [parts.lightness.as_str(), parts.chroma.as_str(), parts.hue.as_str()]
317	            .iter()
318	            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
319	            .copied()
320	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
321	            .join(" ")
322	    }
323	}
324	```

402	/// Get the current value of a single channel from a ColorValue.
403	pub fn channel_value(color: &ColorValue, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {
404	    match channel {
405	        ColorChannel::Hue => color.hue,
406	        ColorChannel::Saturation => color.saturation,
407	        ColorChannel::Lightness => color.lightness,
408	        ColorChannel::Brightness => color.to_hsb().2,
409	        ColorChannel::Alpha => color.alpha,
410	        ColorChannel::Red => color.to_rgb().0 as f64,
411	        ColorChannel::Green => color.to_rgb().1 as f64,
412	        ColorChannel::Blue => color.to_rgb().2 as f64,
413	    }
414	}
415	
416	/// Return a new ColorValue with one channel replaced.
417	pub fn with_channel(color: &ColorValue, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) -> ColorValue {
418	    match channel {
419	        ColorChannel::Hue => ColorValue::new(value, color.saturation, color.lightness, color.alpha),
420	        ColorChannel::Saturation => ColorValue::new(color.hue, value, color.lightness, color.alpha),
421	        ColorChannel::Lightness => ColorValue::new(color.hue, color.saturation, value, color.alpha),
422	        ColorChannel::Brightness => {
423	            // Convert current HSL to HSB, replace B, convert back
424	            let (h, s_hsb, _) = color.to_hsb();
425	            let v = value.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
426	            let l = v * (1.0 - s_hsb / 2.0);
427	            let s_hsl = if l == 0.0 || l == 1.0 { 0.0 } else { (v - l) / l.min(1.0 - l) };
428	            ColorValue::new(h, s_hsl, l, color.alpha)
429	        }
430	        ColorChannel::Alpha => ColorValue::new(color.hue, color.saturation, color.lightness, value),
431	        ColorChannel::Red => {
432	            let (_, g, b) = color.to_rgb();
433	            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(value.round() as u8, g, b);
434	            c.alpha = color.alpha;
435	            c
436	        }
437	        ColorChannel::Green => {
438	            let (r, _, b) = color.to_rgb();
439	            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(r, value.round() as u8, b);
440	            c.alpha = color.alpha;
441	            c
442	        }
443	        ColorChannel::Blue => {
444	            let (r, g, _) = color.to_rgb();
445	            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(r, g, value.round() as u8);
446	            c.alpha = color.alpha;
447	            c
448	        }
449	    }
450	}
451	
452	/// (min, max) range for a channel.
453	pub fn channel_range(channel: ColorChannel) -> (f64, f64) {
454	    match channel {
455	        ColorChannel::Hue => (0.0, 360.0),
456	        ColorChannel::Red | ColorChannel::Green | ColorChannel::Blue => (0.0, 255.0),
457	        _ => (0.0, 1.0), // Saturation, Lightness, Brightness, Alpha
458	    }
459	}

463	    match channel {
464	        ColorChannel::Hue => 1.0,        // 1 degree
465	        ColorChannel::Red | ColorChannel::Green | ColorChannel::Blue => 1.0,
466	        _ => 0.01,                        // 1% for 0..1 range channels
467	    }
468	}

470	/// Strip a functional notation call: `name(...)` -> inner content.
471	fn strip_fn_call<'a>(input: &'a str, name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
472	    let stripped = input.strip_prefix(name)?;
473	    let stripped = stripped.strip_prefix('(')?.strip_suffix(')')?;
474	
475	    Some(stripped)
476	}
477	
478	/// Parse "r, g, b" or "r, g, b, a" inside rgb()/rgba().
479	fn parse_rgb_args(inner: &str, has_alpha: bool) -> Option<ColorValue> {
480	    let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect();
481	    if has_alpha && parts.len() != 4 { return None; }
482	    if !has_alpha && parts.len() != 3 { return None; }
483	    let r: u8 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;
484	    let g: u8 = parts[1].parse().ok()?;
485	    let b: u8 = parts[2].parse().ok()?;
486	    let a: f64 = if has_alpha { parts[3].parse().ok()? } else { 1.0 };
487	
488	    ColorValue::from_rgb(r, g, b).map(|mut c| { c.alpha = a.clamp(0.0, 1.0); c })
489	}
490	
491	/// Parse "h, s%, l%" or "h, s%, l%, a" inside hsl()/hsla().
492	fn parse_hsl_args(inner: &str, has_alpha: bool) -> Option<ColorValue> {
493	    let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect();
494	    if has_alpha && parts.len() != 4 { return None; }
495	    if !has_alpha && parts.len() != 3 { return None; }
496	    let h: f64 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;
497	    let s: f64 = parts[1].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0;
498	    let l: f64 = parts[2].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0;
499	    let a: f64 = if has_alpha { parts[3].parse().ok()? } else { 1.0 };
500	
501	    Some(ColorValue::new(h, s, l, a.clamp(0.0, 1.0)))
502	}
503	
504	/// Parse "h, s%, b%" inside hsb() or "h, s%, b%, a" inside hsba().
505	fn parse_hsb_args(inner: &str, has_alpha: bool) -> Option<ColorValue> {
506	    let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect();
507	    let expected = if has_alpha { 4 } else { 3 };
508	    if parts.len() != expected { return None; }
509	    let h: f64 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;
510	    // Clamp the HSB channels to `0..=1` before the conversion so out-of-range
511	    // input (e.g. `200%`) doesn't skew lightness/saturation and lose the hue.
512	    let s: f64 = (parts[1].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
513	    let b: f64 = (parts[2].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
514	    let a: f64 = if has_alpha { parts[3].parse().ok()? } else { 1.0 };
515	    // Convert HSB -> HSL: lightness = b * (1 - s/2)
516	    let l = b * (1.0 - s / 2.0);
517	    let sl = if l > 0.0 && l < 1.0 { (b - l) / l.min(1.0 - l) } else { 0.0 };
518	
519	    Some(ColorValue::new(h, sl, l, a.clamp(0.0, 1.0)))
520	}
521	
522	/// Parse a user-typed string into a ColorValue.
523	/// Recognizes: "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa", "rgb(r,g,b)", "rgba(r,g,b,a)",
524	/// "hsl(h,s%,l%)", "hsla(h,s%,l%,a)", "hsb(h,s%,b%)".
525	pub fn parse_color_string(input: &str) -> Option<ColorValue> {
526	    let trimmed = input.trim();
527	    if trimmed.starts_with('#') {
528	        return ColorValue::from_hex(trimmed);
529	    }
530	    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "rgba") {
531	        return parse_rgb_args(inner, true);
532	    }
533	    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "rgb") {
534	        return parse_rgb_args(inner, false);
535	    }
536	    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "hsla") {
537	        return parse_hsl_args(inner, true);
538	    }
539	    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "hsl") {
540	        return parse_hsl_args(inner, false);
541	    }
542	    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "hsba") {
543	        return parse_hsb_args(inner, true);
544	    }
545	    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "hsb") {
546	        return parse_hsb_args(inner, false);
547	    }
548	
549	    None
550	}
551	
552	/// Format a ColorValue as a string in the given format.
553	pub fn format_color_string(color: &ColorValue, format: ColorFormat) -> String {
554	    match format {
555	        ColorFormat::Hex => color.to_hex(color.alpha < 1.0),
556	        ColorFormat::Rgb => {
557	            let (r, g, b) = color.to_rgb();
558	            if color.alpha < 1.0 {
559	                format!("rgba({}, {}, {}, {:.2})", r, g, b, color.alpha)
560	            } else {
561	                format!("rgb({}, {}, {})", r, g, b)
562	            }
563	        }
564	        ColorFormat::Hsl => color.to_css_hsl(),
565	        ColorFormat::Hsb => {
566	            let (h, s, b) = color.to_hsb();
567	            // Emit `hsba(...)` for translucent colors so alpha round-trips
568	            // through the parser instead of being silently dropped to opaque.
569	            if color.alpha < 1.0 {
570	                format!("hsba({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%, {:.2})", h, s * 100.0, b * 100.0, color.alpha)
571	            } else {
572	                format!("hsb({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)", h, s * 100.0, b * 100.0)
573	            }
574	        }
575	    }
576	}
577	```
578	
579	### Supported Color Spaces and Conversion
580	
581	**Minimum supported color spaces**: HSL, HSB (HSV), RGB, HEX.
582	
583	| Space | To                                | From                              | Notes                     |
584	| ----- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
585	| HSL   | (native storage)                  | `ColorValue::new(h, s, l, a)`     | Canonical internal format |
586	| RGB   | `to_rgb() -> (u8, u8, u8)`        | `from_rgb(r, g, b) -> Self`       | 0-255 per channel         |
587	| HEX   | `to_hex(include_alpha) -> String` | `from_hex(hex) -> Option<Self>`   | `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`  |
588	| HSB   | `to_hsb() -> (f64, f64, f64)`     | via `with_channel(Brightness, v)` | Hue shared with HSL       |
589	| CSS   | `to_css_hsl() -> String`          | --                                | `hsl()`/`hsla()` string   |
590	
591	Color space conversion rules:
592	
593	1. Out-of-gamut values are clamped to the target color space's valid range during conversion (e.g., HSL saturation > 100% clamped to 100%).
594	2. Channel values are rounded to the precision appropriate for the color space: RGB channels to integers (0-255), HSL/HSB hue to 1 decimal place, saturation/lightness to integers.
595	3. When switching color spaces in the UI, the displayed value is the conversion result of the current color -- no rounding trip-loss accumulation (convert from stored high-precision internal representation each time).
596

869	### 1.6 Color Space Switching
870	
871	`ColorPicker` supports runtime color space switching via `Event::ChangeColorSpace(ColorSpace)`.
872	
873	**Transition Behavior** for `ChangeColorSpace(new_space)`:
874	
875	1. **Recompute value**: Convert the current color value from the old color space to `new_space`. Preserve perceptual magnitudes where possible (e.g., HSL->HSB preserves hue and saturation, converts lightness to brightness).
876	2. **Update context**: Set `ctx.color_space = new_space`. Update `ctx.value` with the converted color.
877	3. **Remap channels**: The color area and channel sliders update to reflect the new space's channels (e.g., switching from RGB to HSL changes the area from Red/Green to Hue/Saturation, and the slider from Blue to Lightness).
878	4. **Live region announcement**: Emit an `aria-live="polite"` announcement: `"Switched to {space} color space"` (e.g., "Switched to HSL color space"). This informs screen reader users that the control layout has changed.
879	
880	**UI Affordance**: The color space selector (button group, dropdown, or segmented control) emits `Event::ChangeColorSpace(selected_space)` when the user selects a different space. The spec does not prescribe a specific UI pattern -- adapters choose the appropriate control.
881	
882	**Supported Spaces**: All spaces in the `ColorSpace` enum (RGB, HSL, HSB/HSV, HEX) are switchable at runtime. The conversion between spaces is lossless for the sRGB gamut (minor floating-point rounding is acceptable).
883	
884	### 1.7 Full Machine Implementation
885	
886	```rust
887	/// Apply a pointer position to the color value for the given drag target.
888	/// For Area: x maps to saturation, y maps to lightness (inverted: top=light).
889	/// For Channel: x maps to the channel's full range via `with_channel()`.
890	fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {
891	    let current = ctx.value.get().clone();
892	    match target {
893	        DragTarget::Area => {
894	            // x maps to saturation [0.0, 1.0], y maps to lightness [1.0, 0.0]
895	            let s = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
896	            let l = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
897	            ctx.value.set(ColorValue::new(current.hue, s, l, current.alpha));
898	        }
899	        DragTarget::Channel(ch) => {
900	            let (min, max) = channel_range(ch);
901	            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);
902	            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&current, ch, value));
903	        }
904	    }
905	}

976	    fn transition(
977	        state: &Self::State,
978	        event: &Self::Event,

980	        props: &Self::Props,

982	        // Global guard: disabled components ignore all events except Focus/Blur.
983	        if ctx.disabled {
984	            return match event {
985	                Event::Focus { part } => {
986	                    let part = *part;
987	                    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
988	                        ctx.focused_part = Some(part);
989	                    }))
990	                }
991	                Event::Blur { .. } => {
992	                    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx| {
993	                        ctx.focused_part = None;
994	                    }))
995	                }

1000	        match (state, event) {
1001	            // --- Closed state ---
1002	            (State::Closed, Event::Open)

1004	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Open).apply(|ctx| {
1005	                    ctx.open.set(true);
1006	                }).with_named_effect("click-outside", |ctx, _props, send| {
1007	                    let content_id = ctx.content_id.clone();

1015	                    cleanup
1016	                }).with_named_effect("detect-eyedropper", |ctx, _props, _send| {

1019	                    // Store result -- in practice this would set context
1020	                    no_cleanup()
1021	                }))
1022	            }
1023	
1024	            // --- Open state ---
1025	            (State::Open, Event::Close)
1026	            | (State::Open, Event::Toggle) => {
1027	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Closed).apply(|ctx| {
1028	                    ctx.open.set(false);
1029	                }))
1030	            }
1031	
1032	            (State::Open, Event::CloseOnInteractOutside) => {
1033	                if ctx.close_on_interact_outside {

1035	                        ctx.open.set(false);

1055	                }

1061	                let x = *x;
1062	                let y = *y;

1071	                        Box::new(move || { send_up.call_if_alive(Event::DragEnd); }),
1072	                    )
1073	                }))
1074	            }
1075	
1076	            // --- Dragging state ---
1077	            (State::Dragging { target }, Event::DragMove { x, y }) => {
1078	                let target = *target;
1079	
1080	                let x = *x;
1081	                let y = *y;
1082	
1083	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
1084	                    apply_drag_position(ctx, target, x, y);

1086	            }

1089	                let final_color = ctx.value.get().clone();

1152	                let step = *step;

1166	                let channel = *channel;
1167	
1168	                let step = *step;

1475	    /// Attributes for a channel slider container. `channel` identifies which
1476	    /// channel this slider controls (e.g., `ColorChannel::Hue`).
1477	    pub fn channel_slider_attrs(&self, channel: ColorChannel) -> AttrMap {
1478	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
1479	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::ChannelSlider { channel }.data_attrs();
1480	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
1481	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
1482	        let slider_id = match channel {
1483	            ColorChannel::Hue => &self.ctx.hue_slider_id,
1484	            ColorChannel::Alpha => &self.ctx.alpha_slider_id,
1485	            _ => &self.ctx.hue_slider_id, // fallback
1486	        };
1487	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, slider_id);
1488	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, "group");
1489	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-channel"), match channel {
1490	            ColorChannel::Hue => "hue",
1491	            ColorChannel::Alpha => "alpha",
1492	            _ => "hue",
1493	        });
1494	        attrs
1495	    }

1497	    /// Attributes for the channel slider thumb (the draggable handle).
1498	    pub fn channel_slider_thumb_attrs(&self, channel: ColorChannel) -> AttrMap {
1499	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
1500	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::ChannelSliderThumb { channel }.data_attrs();
1501	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
1502	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
1503	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, "slider");
1504	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, "0");
1505	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-channel"), match channel {
1506	            ColorChannel::Hue => "hue",
1507	            ColorChannel::Alpha => "alpha",
1508	            _ => "hue",
1509	        });
1510	        let color = self.ctx.value.get();
1511	        let value = channel_value(color, channel);
1512	        let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);
1513	        let label = match channel {
1514	            ColorChannel::Hue => (self.ctx.messages.hue_label)(&self.ctx.locale),
1515	            ColorChannel::Alpha => (self.ctx.messages.alpha_label)(&self.ctx.locale),
1516	            _ => (self.ctx.messages.hue_label)(&self.ctx.locale),
1517	        };
1518	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label);
1519	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueNow), format!("{:.0}", value));
1520	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMin), format!("{:.0}", min));
1521	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMax), format!("{:.0}", max));
1522	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Orientation), "horizontal");
1523	        let pct = if (max - min).abs() > f64::EPSILON { (value - min) / (max - min) * 100.0 } else { 0.0 };
1524	        attrs.set_style(CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-picker-channel-thumb-position"), format!("{:.1}%", pct));
1525	        if matches!(self.state, State::Dragging { target: DragTarget::Channel(c) } if *c == channel) {
1526	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-dragging"), true);
1527	        }
1528	        // Event handlers (keydown for arrow/Home/End channel adjustment) are typed methods on the Api struct.
1529	        attrs
1530	    }

1624	    /// The attributes for the eye dropper trigger element.
1625	    pub fn eye_dropper_trigger_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
1626	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
1627	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::EyeDropperTrigger.data_attrs();
1628	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
1629	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
1630	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), (self.ctx.messages.eyedropper_label)(&self.ctx.locale));
1631	        if !self.ctx.eyedropper_supported {
1632	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Hidden, true);
1633	        }
1634	        if self.ctx.disabled || self.ctx.readonly {
1635	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);

1638	        attrs

1640	
1641	    // **Browser support:** The EyeDropper API is Chromium-only (Chrome 95+, Edge 95+).
1642	    // `eyedropper_supported` MUST be set via runtime detection (`"EyeDropper" in window`).
1643	    // When `false`, the EyeDropper trigger MUST NOT be rendered.
1644	    // The adapter MUST call `EyeDropper.open()` directly from a click event handler
1645	    // (within user gesture, not from an async callback) to satisfy the transient
1646	    // activation requirement. The API is not available in Firefox or Safari.
1647	
1648	    /// The attributes for the hidden input element.
1649	    pub fn hidden_input_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
1650	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
1651	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::HiddenInput.data_attrs();
1652	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
1653	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
1654	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Type, "hidden");
1655	        if let Some(ref name) = self.props.name {
1656	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Name, name);
1657	        }
1658	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Value, self.ctx.value.get().to_hex(self.ctx.show_alpha));
1659	        attrs
1660	    }
1661	}

1733	## 3. Accessibility
1734	
1735	### 3.1 ARIA Roles, States, and Properties
1736	
1737	| Attribute / Behaviour               | Element                | Value                         |
1738	| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- |
1739	| `role="dialog"`                     | `Content`              | Popover container             |
1740	| `aria-haspopup="dialog"`            | `Trigger`              | Indicates popover             |
1741	| `aria-expanded`                     | `Trigger`              | `"true"` / `"false"`          |
1742	| `aria-controls`                     | `Trigger`              | Content ID                    |
1743	| `aria-labelledby`                   | `Content`, `Trigger`   | Label ID                      |
1744	| `role="application"`                | `AreaThumb`            | 2D color area interaction     |
1745	| `aria-roledescription="color area"` | `AreaThumb`            | Describes the 2D area control |
1746	| `role="slider"`                     | Channel slider thumbs  | Slider interaction            |
1747	| `aria-valuenow`                     | Channel slider thumbs  | Current numeric value         |
1748	| `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax`   | Channel slider thumbs  | Channel range                 |
1749	| `aria-valuetext`                    | `AreaThumb`            | Formatted color string        |
1750	| `aria-label`                        | `AreaThumb`            | `"Color area selector"`       |
1751	| `aria-label`                        | Channel slider thumbs  | `"Hue"`, `"Alpha"`            |
1752	| `aria-label`                        | `EyeDropperTrigger`    | `"Pick color from screen"`    |
1753	| `aria-label`                        | `FormatSelect`         | `"Toggle color format"`       |
1754	| `aria-label`                        | `Swatch`               | `"Select color #rrggbb"`      |
1755	| `aria-live="polite"`                | Value text live region | Announces color changes       |
1756	| `aria-disabled="true"`              | `Trigger`              | When disabled                 |
1757	| `aria-keyshortcuts`                 | `AreaThumb`            | Documents arrow key controls  |
1758	
1759	### 3.2 Keyboard Interaction
1760	
1761	| Key         | Element                     | Action                      |
1762	| ----------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------- |
1763	| Enter/Space | `Trigger`                   | Toggle popover              |
1764	| Enter/Space | `Swatch`                    | Select swatch color         |
1765	| Escape      | `Content`                   | Close popover               |
1766	| Arrow keys  | `AreaThumb`                 | Adjust saturation/lightness |
1767	| Shift+Arrow | `AreaThumb`, channel slider | Large step adjustment       |
1768	| Arrow keys  | Channel slider thumbs       | Adjust channel value        |
1769	| Home/End    | Channel slider thumbs       | Jump to min/max             |
1770	| Tab         | All interactive parts       | Standard focus navigation   |
1771	
1772	### 3.3 Screen Reader Announcements
1773	
1774	During keyboard-driven color adjustments, a debounced `aria-live="polite"` announcement (500ms after last keyboard interaction) reads the current color value in the active format (e.g., "Color: #ff3366"). The `Messages` struct includes `color_announcement: MessageFn<dyn Fn(&ColorValue, ColorFormat, &Locale) -> String + Send + Sync>` for this purpose.
1775	
1776	When switching color spaces (via `Event::ChangeColorSpace`), an `aria-live="polite"` announcement reads `"Switched to {space} color space"` to inform screen reader users that the control layout has changed.
1777

1840	| `color_picker.swatch_label`        | `"Select color {color}"`   | Swatch button label (templated) |
1841	
1842	- **RTL**: Channel sliders reverse direction; the area gradient flips horizontally so
1843	  that right-to-left reading order places higher saturation on the leading edge.
1844	- **Number formatting**: Channel input values respect locale decimal separators when
1845	  formatting display values (e.g., `"0,75"` vs `"0.75"`).
1846	
1847	## 5. Variant: Eyedropper
1848	
1849	The EyeDropper API integration is a browser-dependent variant that adds screen color sampling capability.
1850	
1851	### 5.1 Behavior
1852	
1853	- The `eyedropper_supported` context field is set via runtime detection (`"EyeDropper" in window`) during the `detect-eyedropper` effect when the picker opens.
1854	- When `eyedropper_supported` is `false`, the `EyeDropperTrigger` part is hidden (`hidden` attribute set).
1855	- `Event::EyedropperRequest` is only processed when `eyedropper_supported` is `true` and the component is not `readonly`.
1856	- The adapter calls `EyeDropper.open()` directly from a click event handler (within user gesture, not from an async callback) to satisfy the transient activation requirement.
1857	- On success, `Event::EyedropperResult(Some(color))` updates the current value. On cancellation, `Event::EyedropperResult(None)` is sent and no change occurs.
1858	
1859	### 5.2 Anatomy Additions
1860	
1861	The `EyeDropperTrigger` part is conditionally rendered based on browser support. See the `Part::EyeDropperTrigger` variant in the Part enum.
1862	
1863	### 5.3 Accessibility
1864	
1865	The eyedropper trigger button uses `aria-label` from `messages.eyedropper_label` (default: "Pick color from screen"). When the API is unavailable, the button is hidden from both visual and accessibility trees via the `hidden` attribute.
1866	
1867	**Browser support:** The EyeDropper API is Chromium-only (Chrome 95+, Edge 95+). Not available in Firefox or Safari.
1868	
1869	## 6. Library Parity
1870	
1871	> Compared against: Ark UI (`ColorPicker`), React Aria (`ColorPicker`).
1872	
1873	### 6.1 Props
1874	
1875	| Feature                    | ars-ui                    | Ark UI                     | React Aria               | Notes                                                        |
1876	| -------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1877	| `value` / `defaultValue`   | `value` / `default_value` | `value` / `defaultValue`   | `value` / `defaultValue` | Equivalent                                                   |
1878	| `format` / `defaultFormat` | `default_format`          | `format` / `defaultFormat` | --                       | Ark has controlled format; ars-ui uses `Event::SetFormat`    |
1879	| `open` / `defaultOpen`     | `open` / `default_open`   | `open` / `defaultOpen`     | --                       | Equivalent                                                   |
1880	| `disabled`                 | `disabled`                | `disabled`                 | --                       | Equivalent                                                   |
1881	| `readOnly`                 | `readonly`                | `readOnly`                 | --                       | Equivalent                                                   |
1882	| `invalid`                  | --                        | `invalid`                  | --                       | Ark-only; ars-ui validates at form level                     |
1883	| `required`                 | --                        | `required`                 | --                       | Ark-only; ars-ui validates at form level                     |
1884	| `closeOnSelect`            | --                        | `closeOnSelect`            | --                       | Ark-only; ars-ui leaves swatch selection behavior to adapter |
1885	| `inline`                   | --                        | `inline`                   | --                       | Ark-only; ars-ui renders via open state                      |
1886	| `name`                     | `name`                    | `name`                     | --                       | Equivalent                                                   |
1887	| `positioning`              | `positioning`             | `positioning`              | --                       | Equivalent                                                   |
1888	| `colorSpace`               | `color_space`             | --                         | --                       | ars-ui exclusive                                             |
1889	| `showAlpha`                | `show_alpha`              | --                         | --                       | ars-ui exclusive                                             |
1890	| `on_change_end`            | `on_change_end`           | `onValueChangeEnd`         | `onChange`               | Equivalent intent                                            |
1891	
1892	**Gaps:** None worth adopting. `invalid`/`required` are form-level concerns. `closeOnSelect`/`inline` are minor UX preferences best handled in the adapter.
1893	
1894	### 6.2 Anatomy
1895	
1896	| Part               | ars-ui               | Ark UI                           | React Aria                     | Notes                                              |
1897	| ------------------ | -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
1898	| Root               | `Root`               | `Root`                           | `ColorPicker`                  | Equivalent                                         |
1899	| Label              | `Label`              | `Label`                          | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1900	| Control            | `Control`            | `Control`                        | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1901	| Trigger            | `Trigger`            | `Trigger`                        | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1902	| Content            | `Content`            | `Content`                        | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1903	| Area               | `Area`               | `Area`                           | (separate `ColorArea`)         | Equivalent                                         |
1904	| AreaThumb          | `AreaThumb`          | `AreaThumb`                      | `ColorThumb`                   | Equivalent                                         |
1905	| ChannelSlider      | `ChannelSlider`      | `ChannelSlider`                  | (separate `ColorSlider`)       | Equivalent                                         |
1906	| ChannelSliderThumb | `ChannelSliderThumb` | `ChannelSliderThumb`             | `ColorThumb`                   | Equivalent                                         |
1907	| AlphaSlider        | `AlphaSlider`        | (via ChannelSlider)              | --                             | ars-ui has dedicated alpha part                    |
1908	| SwatchGroup        | `SwatchGroup`        | `SwatchGroup`                    | (separate `ColorSwatchPicker`) | Equivalent                                         |
1909	| Swatch             | `Swatch`             | `Swatch`                         | `ColorSwatch`                  | Equivalent                                         |
1910	| FormatSelect       | `FormatSelect`       | `FormatSelect` / `FormatTrigger` | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1911	| ChannelInput       | `ChannelInput`       | `ChannelInput`                   | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1912	| HexInput           | `HexInput`           | --                               | --                             | ars-ui exclusive                                   |
1913	| EyeDropperTrigger  | `EyeDropperTrigger`  | `EyeDropperTrigger`              | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1914	| HiddenInput        | `HiddenInput`        | `HiddenInput`                    | --                             | Equivalent                                         |
1915	| TransparencyGrid   | --                   | `TransparencyGrid`               | --                             | Ark-only; adapter CSS concern                      |
1916	| ValueText          | --                   | `ValueText`                      | --                             | Ark-only; covered by `value_as_string()` on Api    |
1917	| ValueSwatch        | --                   | `ValueSwatch`                    | --                             | Ark-only; adapter can render via trigger           |
1918	| View               | --                   | `View`                           | --                             | Ark-only; format-specific views handled by adapter |
1919	
1920	**Gaps:** None. `TransparencyGrid`, `ValueText`, `ValueSwatch`, and `View` are rendering/layout concerns handled by adapters, not core anatomy.
1921	
1922	### 6.3 Events
1923	
1924	| Callback         | ars-ui                      | Ark UI             | React Aria | Notes                  |
1925	| ---------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------- | ---------------------- |
1926	| Value change     | `Bindable` reactivity       | `onValueChange`    | `onChange` | Equivalent via binding |
1927	| Value change end | `on_change_end`             | `onValueChangeEnd` | --         | Equivalent             |
1928	| Open change      | `Bindable<bool>` reactivity | `onOpenChange`     | --         | Equivalent via binding |
1929	| Format change    | `Event::SetFormat`          | `onFormatChange`   | --         | Equivalent             |
1930	
1931	**Gaps:** None.
1932	
1933	### 6.4 Features
1934	
1935	| Feature               | ars-ui                 | Ark UI         | React Aria           |
1936	| --------------------- | ---------------------- | -------------- | -------------------- |
1937	| Multiple color spaces | Yes (HSL/HSB/RGB/HEX)  | Yes            | Yes                  |
1938	| Color space switching | Yes (runtime)          | Yes (via View) | --                   |
1939	| Eyedropper API        | Yes                    | Yes            | --                   |
1940	| Swatch presets        | Yes                    | Yes            | --                   |
1941	| Alpha channel         | Yes (`show_alpha`)     | Yes            | --                   |
1942	| Keyboard interaction  | Yes (full)             | Yes            | Yes                  |
1943	| RTL support           | Yes                    | Yes            | --                   |
1944	| Color name (a11y)     | Yes (`ColorNameParts`) | --             | Yes (`getColorName`) |
1945	| Contrast ratio utils  | Yes (`contrast_ratio`) | --             | --                   |
1946	
1947	**Gaps:** None.
1948	
1949	### 6.5 Summary
1950	
1951	- **Overall:** Full parity.
1952	- **Divergences:** Ark UI uses a monolithic ColorPicker with sub-parts; ars-ui separates ColorArea, ColorSlider, ColorWheel, ColorField, ColorSwatch, and ColorSwatchPicker as independent components that can also be composed inside ColorPicker. React Aria follows the same separated approach.
1953	- **Recommended additions:** None.

1	//! `ColorArea` component state machine and connect API.
2	//!
3	//! `ColorArea` is a 2D color picker: the thumb position maps to two color
4	//! channels (x and y). It owns the channel math, value state, keyboard
5	//! behavior, and ARIA/data attributes. Live area measurement, pointer capture,
6	//! and coordinate-to-value conversion are adapter concerns: the adapter
7	//! supplies already-normalized `(x, y)` in `0..=1` via [`Api::on_background_pointer_down`]
8	//! (drag start) and drives [`Event::DragMove`] / [`Event::DragEnd`] from its own
9	//! pointer listeners, exactly as the slider does.

273	/// Format a single channel reading for `aria-valuetext`, including the channel
274	/// name and a channel-appropriate unit (degrees for hue, raw for the 8-bit RGB
275	/// channels, a percentage for the fractional channels).
276	fn format_axis_reading(channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) -> String {
277	    let name = format!("{channel:?}").to_lowercase();
278	
279	    match channel {
280	        ColorChannel::Hue => format!("{name} {value:.0}°"),
281	        ColorChannel::Red | ColorChannel::Green | ColorChannel::Blue => {
282	            format!("{name} {value:.0}")
283	        }
284	        _ => format!("{name} {:.0}%", value * 100.0),
285	    }
286	}
287	
288	/// Apply normalized `(x, y)` coordinates to both channels (y is inverted: top = max).
289	fn apply_area_position(ctx: &mut Context, x: f64, y: f64) {
290	    let (x_min, x_max) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);
291	    let (y_min, y_max) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);
292	
293	    // RTL renders the minimum x on the right and mirrors the x-axis arrows, so
294	    // the incoming physical x is inverted to match (left edge selects max).
295	    let x_norm = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
296	    let x_norm = if ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl {
297	        1.0 - x_norm
298	    } else {
299	        x_norm
300	    };
301	
302	    let x_val = x_min + x_norm * (x_max - x_min);
303	    let y_val = y_max - y.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (y_max - y_min);
304	
305	    ctx.x_value = x_val;
306	    ctx.y_value = y_val;
307	
308	    // Apply both channels from the pending color in a single read. Reading
309	    // `get()` in controlled mode returns the stale prop, and reading the bindable
310	    // twice (as two `set_*_value` calls) would discard the first change.
311	    let color = *ctx.value.pending();
312	    let updated = with_channel(&color, ctx.x_channel, x_val);
313	    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, ctx.y_channel, y_val));
314	}
315	
316	/// Set the x-axis channel value (unwrapped) and derive the color from it.
317	///
318	/// Bases the new color on the *pending* value so a prior single-axis change
319	/// (e.g. an earlier `IncrementY`) is preserved in controlled mode, where
320	/// `get()` still returns the unchanged controlled prop.
321	fn set_x_value(ctx: &mut Context, value: f64) {
322	    ctx.x_value = value;
323	
324	    let color = *ctx.value.pending();
325	    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&color, ctx.x_channel, value));
326	}
327	
328	/// Set the y-axis channel value (unwrapped) and derive the color from it.
329	///
330	/// Bases the new color on the *pending* value (see [`set_x_value`]).
331	fn set_y_value(ctx: &mut Context, value: f64) {
332	    ctx.y_value = value;
333	
334	    let color = *ctx.value.pending();
335	    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&color, ctx.y_channel, value));
336	}
337	
338	/// Build the change-end effect that invokes `Props::on_change_end`.
339	///
340	/// Reports the *pending* value staged during the drag rather than the
341	/// controlled `get()` value, which in controlled mode still holds the stale
342	/// pre-drag color until the parent syncs the new value back through its prop.
343	fn change_end_effect() -> PendingEffect<Machine> {
344	    PendingEffect::new(Effect::ChangeEnd, |ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {
345	        if let Some(callback) = &props.on_change_end {
346	            callback(*ctx.value.pending());
347	        }
348	
349	        no_cleanup()
350	    })
351	}

353	/// The machine for the `ColorArea` component.
354	#[derive(Debug)]
355	pub struct Machine;
356	
357	impl ars_core::Machine for Machine {
358	    type State = State;
359	    type Event = Event;
360	    type Context = Context;
361	    type Props = Props;
362	    type Messages = Messages;
363	    type Effect = Effect;
364	    type Api<'a> = Api<'a>;
365	
366	    fn init(
367	        props: &Self::Props,
368	        env: &Env,
369	        messages: &Self::Messages,
370	    ) -> (Self::State, Self::Context) {
371	        let value = if let Some(v) = &props.value {
372	            Bindable::controlled(*v)
373	        } else {
374	            Bindable::uncontrolled(props.default_value)
375	        };
376	
377	        let x_value = channel_value(value.get(), props.x_channel);
378	        let y_value = channel_value(value.get(), props.y_channel);
379	
380	        let context = Context {
381	            value,
382	            x_value,
383	            y_value,
384	            x_channel: props.x_channel,
385	            y_channel: props.y_channel,
386	            disabled: props.disabled,
387	            readonly: props.readonly,
388	            focused: false,
389	            focus_visible: false,
390	            step: props.step,
391	            large_step: props.large_step,
392	            dir: props.dir,
393	            locale: env.locale.clone(),
394	            messages: messages.clone(),
395	            ids: ComponentIds::from_id(&props.id),
396	        };
397	
398	        (State::Idle, context)
399	    }
400	
401	    fn transition(
402	        state: &Self::State,
403	        event: &Self::Event,
404	        ctx: &Self::Context,
405	        props: &Self::Props,
406	    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {
407	        // A disabled area ignores value-changing input but still tracks focus
408	        // and accepts parent-driven prop syncs (so it can be re-enabled).
409	        // `DragEnd` is allowed through so a drag in flight when the parent
410	        // disabled the control can still terminate cleanly.
411	        if ctx.disabled {
412	            match event {
413	                Event::DragStart { .. }
414	                | Event::DragMove { .. }
415	                | Event::IncrementX { .. }
416	                | Event::DecrementX { .. }
417	                | Event::IncrementY { .. }
418	                | Event::DecrementY { .. }
419	                | Event::SetXToMin
420	                | Event::SetXToMax
421	                | Event::SetYToMin
422	                | Event::SetYToMax => return None,
423	                _ => {}
424	            }
425	        }
426	
427	        match (state, event) {
428	            (State::Idle, Event::DragStart { x, y }) => {
429	                if ctx.readonly {
430	                    return None;
431	                }
432	
433	                let (x, y) = (*x, *y);
434	                Some(
435	                    TransitionPlan::to(State::Dragging).apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
436	                        apply_area_position(ctx, x, y);
437	                    }),
438	                )
439	            }
440	
441	            (State::Dragging, Event::DragMove { x, y }) => {
442	                // Readonly toggled mid-drag must stop further value changes
443	                // (disabled is already handled by the guard above); DragEnd
444	                // still terminates the drag.
445	                if ctx.readonly {
446	                    return None;
447	                }
448	
449	                let (x, y) = (*x, *y);
450	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
451	                    apply_area_position(ctx, x, y);
452	                }))
453	            }
454	
455	            (State::Dragging, Event::DragEnd) => {
456	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle).with_effect(change_end_effect()))
457	            }
458	
459	            (_, Event::IncrementX { step }) => {
460	                if ctx.readonly {
461	                    return None;
462	                }
463	
464	                let step = *step;
465	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
466	                    let (_, max) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);
467	                    set_x_value(ctx, (ctx.x_value + step).min(max));
468	                }))
469	            }
470	
471	            (_, Event::DecrementX { step }) => {
472	                if ctx.readonly {
473	                    return None;
474	                }
475	
476	                let step = *step;
477	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
478	                    let (min, _) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);
479	                    set_x_value(ctx, (ctx.x_value - step).max(min));
480	                }))
481	            }
482	
483	            (_, Event::IncrementY { step }) => {
484	                if ctx.readonly {
485	                    return None;
486	                }
487	
488	                let step = *step;
489	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
490	                    let (_, max) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);
491	                    set_y_value(ctx, (ctx.y_value + step).min(max));
492	                }))
493	            }
494	
495	            (_, Event::DecrementY { step }) => {
496	                if ctx.readonly {
497	                    return None;
498	                }
499	
500	                let step = *step;
501	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
502	                    let (min, _) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);
503	                    set_y_value(ctx, (ctx.y_value - step).max(min));
504	                }))
505	            }
506	
507	            (_, Event::SetXToMin) => {
508	                if ctx.readonly {
509	                    return None;
510	                }
511	
512	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx: &mut Context| {
513	                    let (min, _) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);
514	                    set_x_value(ctx, min);
515	                }))
516	            }
517	
518	            (_, Event::SetXToMax) => {
519	                if ctx.readonly {
520	                    return None;
521	                }
522	
523	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx: &mut Context| {
524	                    let (_, max) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);
525	                    set_x_value(ctx, max);
526	                }))
527	            }
528	
529	            (_, Event::SetYToMin) => {
530	                if ctx.readonly {
531	                    return None;
532	                }
533	
534	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx: &mut Context| {
535	                    let (min, _) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);
536	                    set_y_value(ctx, min);
537	                }))
538	            }
539	
540	            (_, Event::SetYToMax) => {
541	                if ctx.readonly {
542	                    return None;
543	                }
544	
545	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx: &mut Context| {
546	                    let (_, max) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);
547	                    set_y_value(ctx, max);
548	                }))
549	            }
550	
551	            (_, Event::Focus { is_keyboard }) => {
552	                let kb = *is_keyboard;
553	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
554	                    ctx.focused = true;
555	                    ctx.focus_visible = kb;
556	                }))
557	            }
558	
559	            (_, Event::Blur) => Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx: &mut Context| {
560	                ctx.focused = false;
561	                ctx.focus_visible = false;
562	            })),
563	
564	            (_, Event::SyncValue(value)) => {
565	                let value = *value;
566	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(
567	                    move |ctx: &mut Context| match value {
568	                        Some(color) => {
569	                            // Keep the cached axis values when the parent echoes the
570	                            // value we emitted, so a hue 360° endpoint isn't
571	                            // re-derived back to 0° (the color normalizes 360°->0°).
572	                            let echoes_pending = color == *ctx.value.pending();
573	
574	                            ctx.value.set(color);
575	                            ctx.value.sync_controlled(Some(color));
576	
577	                            if !echoes_pending {
578	                                ctx.x_value = channel_value(&color, ctx.x_channel);
579	                                ctx.y_value = channel_value(&color, ctx.y_channel);
580	                            }
581	                        }
582	                        None => ctx.value.sync_controlled(None),
583	                    },
584	                ))
585	            }
586	
587	            (_, Event::SetProps) => {
588	                let props = props.clone();
589	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
590	                    let x_channel_changed = ctx.x_channel != props.x_channel;
591	                    let y_channel_changed = ctx.y_channel != props.y_channel;
592	
593	                    ctx.x_channel = props.x_channel;
594	                    ctx.y_channel = props.y_channel;
595	                    ctx.step = props.step;
596	                    ctx.large_step = props.large_step;
597	                    ctx.disabled = props.disabled;
598	                    ctx.readonly = props.readonly;
599	                    ctx.dir = props.dir;
600	
601	                    // A new axis channel means the cached axis value refers to the
602	                    // old channel; re-derive it from the current color.
603	                    if x_channel_changed {
604	                        ctx.x_value = channel_value(ctx.value.get(), ctx.x_channel);
605	                    }
606	                    if y_channel_changed {
607	                        ctx.y_value = channel_value(ctx.value.get(), ctx.y_channel);
608	                    }
609	                }))
610	            }
611	
612	            _ => None,
613	        }
614	    }
615	
616	    fn on_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> Vec<Event> {
617	        assert_eq!(
618	            old.id, new.id,
619	            "color_area::Props.id must remain stable after init"
620	        );
621	
622	        let mut events = Vec::new();
623	
624	        if old.value != new.value {
625	            events.push(Event::SyncValue(new.value));
626	        }
627	
628	        if props_output_changed(old, new) {
629	            events.push(Event::SetProps);
630	        }
631	
632	        events
633	    }
634	
635	    fn connect<'a>(
636	        state: &'a Self::State,
637	        ctx: &'a Self::Context,
638	        props: &'a Self::Props,
639	        send: &'a dyn Fn(Self::Event),
640	    ) -> Self::Api<'a> {
641	        Api {
642	            state,
643	            ctx,
644	            props,
645	            send,
646	        }
647	    }
648	}
649	
650	/// Whether any cached output prop changed and the context needs refreshing.
651	///
652	/// `name` is omitted: it is read live from `Props` in `hidden_input_attrs`
653	/// rather than cached in the context.
654	fn props_output_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {
655	    old.x_channel != new.x_channel
656	        || old.y_channel != new.y_channel
657	        || (old.step - new.step).abs() > f64::EPSILON
658	        || (old.large_step - new.large_step).abs() > f64::EPSILON
659	        || old.disabled != new.disabled
660	        || old.readonly != new.readonly
661	        || old.dir != new.dir
662	}
663	
664	/// Structural parts exposed by the `ColorArea` connect API.
665	#[derive(ComponentPart)]
666	#[scope = "color-area"]
667	pub enum Part {
668	    /// Container with `role="group"`.
669	    Root,
670	
671	    /// 2D gradient background.
672	    Background,
673	
674	    /// Draggable thumb with `role="application"`.
675	    Thumb,
676	
677	    /// `type="hidden"` input that submits the hex value for forms.
678	    HiddenInput,
679	}
680	
681	/// The connect API for the `ColorArea` component.
682	pub struct Api<'a> {
683	    state: &'a State,
684	    ctx: &'a Context,
685	    props: &'a Props,
686	    send: &'a dyn Fn(Event),
687	}
688	
689	impl Debug for Api<'_> {
690	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
691	        f.debug_struct("color_area::Api")
692	            .field("state", &self.state)
693	            .field("ctx", &self.ctx)
694	            .finish_non_exhaustive()
695	    }
696	}
697	
698	impl Api<'_> {
699	    /// Whether the thumb is currently being dragged.
700	    #[must_use]
701	    pub const fn is_dragging(&self) -> bool {
702	        matches!(self.state, State::Dragging)
703	    }
704	
705	    /// The current color value.
706	    #[must_use]
707	    pub fn value(&self) -> &ColorValue {
708	        self.ctx.value.get()
709	    }
710	
711	    /// Attributes for the root element.
712	    #[must_use]
713	    pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
714	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
715	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
716	
717	        attrs
718	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
719	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
720	            .set(HtmlAttr::Role, "group");
721	
722	        if self.ctx.disabled {
723	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-disabled"), true);
724	        }
725	
726	        if self.ctx.readonly {
727	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-readonly"), true);
728	        }
729	
730	        if self.is_dragging() {
731	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-dragging"), true);
732	        }
733	
734	        attrs
735	    }
736	
737	    /// Attributes for the gradient background element.
738	    #[must_use]
739	    pub fn background_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
740	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
741	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Background.data_attrs();
742	
743	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val).set(part_attr, part_val);
744	
745	        // Pending color so the background tracks an in-progress controlled drag.
746	        let color = self.ctx.value.pending();
747	
748	        // Dominant hue backdrop (kept for the default saturation×lightness case).
749	        attrs.set_style(
750	            CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-area-bg"),
751	            format!("hsl({:.0}, 100%, 50%)", color.hue),
752	        );
753	
754	        // Expose the configured axes plus the four corner colors so the adapter
755	        // can render a 2D gradient that matches *any* x/y channel pair, not just
756	        // the default surface. Corners are emitted in visual order (top = the
757	        // y-axis maximum since y is inverted; left/right follow the RTL x flip).
758	        let (x_min, x_max) = channel_range(self.ctx.x_channel);
759	        let (y_min, y_max) = channel_range(self.ctx.y_channel);
760	
761	        let (left_x, right_x) = if self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl {
762	            (x_max, x_min)
763	        } else {
764	            (x_min, x_max)
765	        };
766	
767	        let corner = |x_value: f64, y_value: f64| {
768	            let with_x = with_channel(color, self.ctx.x_channel, x_value);
769	            with_channel(&with_x, self.ctx.y_channel, y_value).to_css_hsl()
770	        };
771	
772	        attrs
773	            .set(
774	                HtmlAttr::Data("ars-x-channel"),
775	                format!("{:?}", self.ctx.x_channel).to_lowercase(),
776	            )
777	            .set(
778	                HtmlAttr::Data("ars-y-channel"),
779	                format!("{:?}", self.ctx.y_channel).to_lowercase(),
780	            )
781	            .set_style(
782	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-area-corner-tl"),
783	                corner(left_x, y_max),
784	            )
785	            .set_style(
786	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-area-corner-tr"),
787	                corner(right_x, y_max),
788	            )
789	            .set_style(
790	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-area-corner-bl"),
791	                corner(left_x, y_min),
792	            )
793	            .set_style(
794	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-area-corner-br"),
795	                corner(right_x, y_min),
796	            );
797	
798	        attrs
799	    }

801	    /// Attributes for the draggable thumb element.
802	    #[must_use]
803	    pub fn thumb_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
804	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
805	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Thumb.data_attrs();
806	
807	        attrs
808	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
809	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
810	            .set(HtmlAttr::Id, self.ctx.ids.part("thumb"))
811	            .set(HtmlAttr::Role, "application")
812	            .set(
813	                HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RoleDescription),
814	                (self.ctx.messages.role_description)(&self.ctx.locale),
815	            )
816	            // A disabled control must stay out of the tab order.
817	            .set(
818	                HtmlAttr::TabIndex,
819	                if self.ctx.disabled { "-1" } else { "0" },
820	            )
821	            .set(
822	                HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label),
823	                (self.ctx.messages.label)(&self.ctx.locale),
824	            );
825	
826	        if self.ctx.disabled {
827	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), "true");
828	        }
829	
830	        // Pending color so the thumb background and color name match the
831	        // in-progress drag in controlled mode.
832	        let color = self.ctx.value.pending();
833	
834	        // Unwrapped axis values keep hue endpoints (360°) distinct from 0°.
835	        let x_val = self.ctx.x_value;
836	        let y_val = self.ctx.y_value;
837	
838	        let (x_min, x_max) = channel_range(self.ctx.x_channel);
839	        let (y_min, y_max) = channel_range(self.ctx.y_channel);
840	
841	        let x_reading = format_axis_reading(self.ctx.x_channel, x_val);
842	        let y_reading = format_axis_reading(self.ctx.y_channel, y_val);
843	        let color_name = color.color_name_en();
844	
845	        attrs.set(
846	            HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueText),
847	            (self.ctx.messages.value_text)(&x_reading, &y_reading, &color_name, &self.ctx.locale),
848	        );
849	
850	        let mut x_pct = if (x_max - x_min).abs() > f64::EPSILON {
851	            (x_val - x_min) / (x_max - x_min) * 100.0
852	        } else {
853	            0.0
854	        };
855	
856	        // RTL flips the x gradient horizontally (min on the right), matching the
857	        // mirrored x-axis arrow handling in `on_thumb_keydown`.
858	        if self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl {
859	            x_pct = 100.0 - x_pct;
860	        }
861	
862	        let y_pct = if (y_max - y_min).abs() > f64::EPSILON {
863	            (1.0 - (y_val - y_min) / (y_max - y_min)) * 100.0
864	        } else {
865	            0.0
866	        };
867	
868	        attrs
869	            .set_style(
870	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-area-thumb-x"),
871	                format!("{x_pct:.1}%"),
872	            )
873	            .set_style(
874	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-color-area-thumb-y"),
875	                format!("{y_pct:.1}%"),
876	            )
877	            .set_style(CssProperty::BackgroundColor, color.to_css_hsl())
878	            .set(
879	                HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::KeyShortcuts),
880	                "ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight",
881	            );
882	
883	        if self.is_dragging() {
884	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-dragging"), true);
885	        }
886	
887	        if self.ctx.focus_visible {
888	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-focus-visible"), true);
889	        }
890	
891	        attrs
892	    }
893	
894	    /// Attributes for the hidden form input.
895	    #[must_use]
896	    pub fn hidden_input_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
897	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
898	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::HiddenInput.data_attrs();
899	
900	        attrs
901	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
902	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
903	            .set(HtmlAttr::Type, "hidden");
904	
905	        if let Some(name) = &self.props.name {
906	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Name, name.clone());
907	        }
908	
909	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Value, self.ctx.value.pending().to_hex(true));
910	
911	        // A disabled control must be omitted from form submission.
912	        if self.ctx.disabled {
913	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);
914	        }
915	
916	        attrs
917	    }
918	
919	    /// Handles a keydown on the thumb. `shift` selects the large step.
920	    ///
921	    /// In RTL, the x-axis arrow keys are mirrored so `ArrowLeft` increments and
922	    /// `ArrowRight` decrements; the y-axis and Home/End/PageUp/PageDown are
923	    /// direction-independent.
924	    pub fn on_thumb_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData, shift: bool) {
925	        let step = if shift {
926	            self.ctx.large_step
927	        } else {
928	            self.ctx.step
929	        };
930	
931	        let rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;
932	
933	        match data.key {
934	            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => (self.send)(if rtl {
935	                Event::DecrementX { step }
936	            } else {
937	                Event::IncrementX { step }
938	            }),
939	
940	            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => (self.send)(if rtl {
941	                Event::IncrementX { step }
942	            } else {
943	                Event::DecrementX { step }
944	            }),
945	
946	            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::IncrementY { step }),
947	
948	            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::DecrementY { step }),
949	
950	            KeyboardKey::Home => (self.send)(Event::SetXToMin),
951	
952	            KeyboardKey::End => (self.send)(Event::SetXToMax),
953	
954	            KeyboardKey::PageUp => (self.send)(Event::SetYToMax),
955	
956	            KeyboardKey::PageDown => (self.send)(Event::SetYToMin),
957	
958	            _ => {}
959	        }
960	    }
961	
962	    /// Dispatches a drag-start from an adapter-resolved normalized `(x, y)`.
963	    pub fn on_background_pointer_down(&self, x: f64, y: f64) {
964	        (self.send)(Event::DragStart { x, y });
965	    }
966	}
967	
968	impl ConnectApi for Api<'_> {
969	    type Part = Part;
970	
971	    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Part) -> AttrMap {
972	        match part {
973	            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(),
974	            Part::Background => self.background_attrs(),
975	            Part::Thumb => self.thumb_attrs(),
976	            Part::HiddenInput => self.hidden_input_attrs(),
977	        }
978	    }
979	}

1149	        let flag = Arc::clone(&fired);

1151	            on_change_end: Some(callback(move |_c: ColorValue| {

1159	        let mut end = svc.send(Event::DragEnd);
1160	
1161	        assert_eq!(end.pending_effects.len(), 1);
1162	
1163	        let send: StrongSend<Event> = Arc::new(|_| {});
1164	
1165	        for effect in end.pending_effects.drain(..) {
1166	            drop(effect.run(svc.context(), svc.props(), Arc::clone(&send)));
1167	        }
1168	
1169	        assert!(fired.load(Ordering::SeqCst));
1170	    }

1352	    #[test]
1353	    fn drag_end_reports_pending_value_for_controlled_area() {
1354	        use alloc::sync::Arc;
1355	        use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
1356	
1357	        use ars_core::{StrongSend, callback};
1358	
1359	        let reported = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX));
1360	        let sink = Arc::clone(&reported);
1361	        let mut svc = service(Props {
1362	            // Controlled at saturation 0; a drag must report the new saturation.
1363	            value: Some(ColorValue::from_hsl(0.0, 0.0, 0.5)),
1364	            on_change_end: Some(callback(move |color: ColorValue| {
1365	                sink.store(color.saturation.to_bits(), Ordering::SeqCst);
