875	### 1.6 Color Space Switching
876	
877	`ColorPicker` supports runtime color space switching via `Event::ChangeColorSpace(ColorSpace)`.
878	
879	**Transition Behavior** for `ChangeColorSpace(new_space)`:
880	
881	1. **Recompute value**: Convert the current color value from the old color space to `new_space`. Preserve perceptual magnitudes where possible (e.g., HSL->HSB preserves hue and saturation, converts lightness to brightness).
882	2. **Update context**: Set `ctx.color_space = new_space`. Update `ctx.value` with the converted color.
883	3. **Remap channels**: The color area and channel sliders update to reflect the new space's channels (e.g., switching from RGB to HSL changes the area from Red/Green to Hue/Saturation, and the slider from Blue to Lightness).
884	4. **Live region announcement**: Emit an `aria-live="polite"` announcement: `"Switched to {space} color space"` (e.g., "Switched to HSL color space"). This informs screen reader users that the control layout has changed.
885	
886	**UI Affordance**: The color space selector (button group, dropdown, or segmented control) emits `Event::ChangeColorSpace(selected_space)` when the user selects a different space. The spec does not prescribe a specific UI pattern -- adapters choose the appropriate control.
887	
888	**Supported Spaces**: All spaces in the `ColorSpace` enum (RGB, HSL, HSB/HSV, HEX) are switchable at runtime. The conversion between spaces is lossless for the sRGB gamut (minor floating-point rounding is acceptable).
889

  "content": "### 1.7 Full Machine Implementation\n\nThe machine follows the canonical sibling conventions: controlled/uncontrolled\n`value` and `open` are held in `Bindable`s, side effects are emitted as a typed\n[`Effect`](#) enum (the agnostic core never touches the DOM or browser APIs), and\nparent prop changes flow back through `on_props_changed`. Pointer drag is\n**adapter-driven**: the adapter measures the dragged surface and sends\nalready-normalized `(x, y)` in `0..=1` via `DragStart`/`DragMove`/`DragEnd`,\nexactly as `ColorArea`/`ColorSlider` do, so no element measurement happens inside\na core effect closure.\n\n```rust\n/// Typed identifier for the named side effects the machine emits. Adapters\n/// dispatch on these exhaustively; the core never performs the work itself.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum Effect {\n    /// Invoke `Props::on_change_end` with the final color (fired on `DragEnd`).\n    ChangeEnd,\n    /// Attach the click-outside listener (fired on `Closed → Open` and a\n    /// non-`Closed` initial mount). The adapter dispatches\n    /// `Event::CloseOnInteractOutside` when an outside interaction occurs.\n    AttachClickOutside,\n    /// Detach the click-outside listener (fired on `Open → Closed`).\n    DetachClickOutside,\n    /// Detect browser EyeDropper support (fired on `Closed → Open` and a\n    /// non-`Closed` initial mount). The adapter performs the\n    /// `\"EyeDropper\" in window` check and reports the result via\n    /// `Event::SetEyedropperSupported`.\n    DetectEyedropper,\n    /// Open the browser EyeDropper (fired on `EyedropperRequest`). The adapter\n    /// calls `EyeDropper.open()` from the originating user gesture and reports\n    /// the outcome via `Event::EyedropperResult`.\n    InvokeEyedropper,\n    /// Announce the active color-space change via an `aria-live` region. The\n    /// adapter reads the text from `Api::color_space_announcement`.\n    AnnounceColorSpace,\n}\n\n/// Apply an adapter-normalized pointer position to the color value for the given\n/// drag target. `Area` maps x→saturation `[0, 1]` and y→lightness `[1, 0]`\n/// (top = lightest); `Channel` maps x across the channel's full range. Both base\n/// the new color on the *pending* value so a controlled drag-in-flight\n/// accumulates rather than re-reading the stale controlled prop.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => {\n            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let lightness = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            ctx.value.set(ColorValue::new(current.hue, saturation, lightness, current.alpha));\n        }\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&current, channel, value));\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Invoke `Props::on_change_end` with the pending (drag-staged) color.\nfn change_end_effect() -> PendingEffect<Machine> {\n    PendingEffect::new(Effect::ChangeEnd, |ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {\n        if let Some(callback) = &props.on_change_end {\n            callback(*ctx.value.pending());\n        }\n        no_cleanup()\n    })\n}\n\n/// The named effects produced by the open lifecycle. Shared by `open_plan`\n/// (`Closed → Open`) and `Machine::initial_effects` (booted-open) so the two\n/// entry points stay in lock-step.\nfn open_lifecycle_effects() -> [PendingEffect<Machine>; 2] {\n    [\n        PendingEffect::named(Effect::AttachClickOutside),\n        PendingEffect::named(Effect::DetectEyedropper),\n    ]\n}\n\nfn open_plan() -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Open).apply(|ctx: &mut Context| ctx.open.set(true));\n    for effect in open_lifecycle_effects() {\n        plan = plan.with_effect(effect);\n    }\n    plan\n}\n\nfn close_plan() -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::to(State::Closed)\n        .apply(|ctx: &mut Context| ctx.open.set(false))\n        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::DetachClickOutside))\n}\n\n/// Whether any context-backed non-`value`/`open` prop changed (drives `SetProps`).\nfn context_relevant_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {\n    old.disabled != new.disabled\n        || old.readonly != new.readonly\n        || old.close_on_interact_outside != new.close_on_interact_outside\n        || old.close_on_escape != new.close_on_escape\n        || old.show_alpha != new.show_alpha\n        || old.color_space != new.color_space\n        || old.swatches != new.swatches\n        || old.dir != new.dir\n        || old.positioning != new.positioning\n        || (old.channel_step - new.channel_step).abs() > f64::EPSILON\n        || (old.channel_large_step - new.channel_large_step).abs() > f64::EPSILON\n}\n\n/// The machine for the `ColorPicker` component.\npub struct Machine;\n\nimpl ars_core::Machine for Machine {\n    type State = State;\n    type Event = Event;\n    type Context = Context;\n    type Props = Props;\n    type Messages = Messages;\n    type Effect = Effect;\n    type Api<'a> = Api<'a>;\n\n    fn init(props: &Self::Props, env: &Env, messages: &Self::Messages) -> (Self::State, Self::Context) {\n        let value = match props.value {\n            Some(color) => Bindable::controlled(color),\n            None => Bindable::uncontrolled(props.default_value),\n        };\n        let open = match props.open {\n            Some(open) => Bindable::controlled(open),\n            None => Bindable::uncontrolled(props.default_open),\n        };\n        let state = if *open.get() { State::Open } else { State::Closed };\n\n        (state, Context {\n            value,\n            open,\n            format: props.default_format,\n            disabled: props.disabled,\n            readonly: props.readonly,\n            close_on_interact_outside: props.close_on_interact_outside,\n            close_on_escape: props.close_on_escape,\n            show_alpha: props.show_alpha,\n            eyedropper_supported: false, // adapter reports via SetEyedropperSupported\n            focused_part: None,\n            positioning: props.positioning.clone(),\n            channel_step: props.channel_step,\n            channel_large_step: props.channel_large_step,\n            color_space: props.color_space,\n            swatches: props.swatches.clone(),\n            dir: props.dir,\n            locale: env.locale.clone(),\n            messages: messages.clone(),\n            ids: ComponentIds::from_id(&props.id),\n        })\n    }\n\n    fn transition(\n        state: &Self::State,\n        event: &Self::Event,\n        ctx: &Self::Context,\n        props: &Self::Props,\n    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {\n        // A disabled picker ignores interaction but still tracks focus and\n        // accepts parent-driven prop/value syncs (so it can be re-enabled).\n        if ctx.disabled {\n            match event {\n                Event::Focus { .. } | Event::Blur { .. } | Event::SyncValue(_) | Event::SetProps => {}\n                _ => return None,\n            }\n        }\n\n        match (state, event) {\n            (State::Closed, Event::Open | Event::Toggle) => Some(open_plan()),\n            (State::Open, Event::Close | Event::Toggle) => Some(close_plan()),\n\n            (State::Open, Event::CloseOnInteractOutside) if ctx.close_on_interact_outside => {\n                Some(close_plan())\n            }\n            // Interact-outside is suppressed during a drag (pointer capture active).\n            (State::Dragging { .. }, Event::CloseOnInteractOutside) => None,\n            (State::Open, Event::CloseOnEscape) if ctx.close_on_escape => Some(close_plan()),\n\n            (State::Open, Event::DragStart { target, x, y }) => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let (target, x, y) = (*target, *x, *y);\n                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Dragging { target })\n                    .apply(move |ctx| apply_drag_position(ctx, target, x, y)))\n            }\n            (State::Dragging { target }, Event::DragMove { x, y }) => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let (target, x, y) = (*target, *x, *y);\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| apply_drag_position(ctx, target, x, y)))\n            }\n            (State::Dragging { .. }, Event::DragEnd) => {\n                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Open).with_effect(change_end_effect()))\n            }\n\n            (_, Event::SetColor(color)) => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let color = *color;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.value.set(color)))\n            }\n            (State::Open, Event::SetChannel { channel, value }) => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let (channel, value) = (*channel, *value);\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    let color = *ctx.value.pending();\n                    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&color, channel, value));\n                }))\n            }\n            (_, Event::SetFormat(format)) => {\n                let format = *format;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.format = format))\n            }\n            (_, Event::ChangeColorSpace(new_space)) => {\n                let new_space = *new_space;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.color_space = new_space)\n                    .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::AnnounceColorSpace)))\n            }\n\n            (State::Open, Event::ChannelIncrement { channel, step }) => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let (channel, step) = (*channel, *step);\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    let color = *ctx.value.pending();\n                    let (_, max) = channel_range(channel);\n                    let next = (channel_value(&color, channel) + step).min(max);\n                    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&color, channel, next));\n                }))\n            }\n            (State::Open, Event::ChannelDecrement { channel, step }) => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let (channel, step) = (*channel, *step);\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    let color = *ctx.value.pending();\n                    let (min, _) = channel_range(channel);\n                    let next = (channel_value(&color, channel) - step).max(min);\n                    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&color, channel, next));\n                }))\n            }\n\n            (State::Open, Event::EyedropperRequest) => {\n                if !ctx.eyedropper_supported || ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|_ctx| {})\n                    .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::InvokeEyedropper)))\n            }\n            (_, Event::EyedropperResult(Some(color))) => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let color = *color;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.value.set(color)))\n            }\n            (_, Event::SetEyedropperSupported(supported)) => {\n                let supported = *supported;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.eyedropper_supported = supported))\n            }\n\n            (_, Event::Focus { part }) => {\n                let part = *part;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.focused_part = Some(part)))\n            }\n            (_, Event::Blur { .. }) => {\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx| ctx.focused_part = None))\n            }\n\n            (_, Event::SyncValue(value)) => {\n                let value = *value;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    if let Some(color) = value { ctx.value.set(color); }\n                    ctx.value.sync_controlled(value);\n                }))\n            }\n            (_, Event::SetProps) => {\n                let props = props.clone();\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.disabled = props.disabled;\n                    ctx.readonly = props.readonly;\n                    ctx.close_on_interact_outside = props.close_on_interact_outside;\n                    ctx.close_on_escape = props.close_on_escape;\n                    ctx.show_alpha = props.show_alpha;\n                    ctx.color_space = props.color_space;\n                    ctx.swatches = props.swatches;\n                    ctx.dir = props.dir;\n                    ctx.positioning = props.positioning;\n                    ctx.channel_step = props.channel_step;\n                    ctx.channel_large_step = props.channel_large_step;\n                }))\n            }\n\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn on_props_changed(old: &Self::Props, new: &Self::Props) -> Vec<Self::Event> {\n        // The id is baked into Context::ids (and every aria-* relationship that\n        // points at it) at init; allowing it to change would break ARIA wiring.\n        assert_eq!(old.id, new.id, \"color_picker::Props.id must remain stable after init\");\n\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n        // A controlled `open` flip drives the same Open/Close transition the user\n        // would, so the lifecycle effects fire identically.\n        if let (was, Some(now)) = (old.open, new.open) && was != Some(now) {\n            events.push(if now { Event::Open } else { Event::Close });\n        }\n        if old.value != new.value {\n            events.push(Event::SyncValue(new.value));\n        }\n        if context_relevant_props_changed(old, new) {\n            events.push(Event::SetProps);\n        }\n        events\n    }\n\n    fn initial_effects(\n        state: &Self::State,\n        _context: &Self::Context,\n        _props: &Self::Props,\n    ) -> Vec<PendingEffect<Self>> {\n        // A `default_open`/controlled-open boot returns `State::Open` from `init`,\n        // so the `Closed → Open` plan never runs. Mirror its lifecycle effects so\n        // adapters drive identical wiring on first mount via `take_initial_effects`.\n        if matches!(state, State::Open) {\n            open_lifecycle_effects().into_iter().collect()\n        } else {\n            Vec::new()\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn connect<'a>(\n        state: &'a Self::State,\n        ctx: &'a Self::Context,\n        props: &'a Self::Props,\n        send: &'a dyn Fn(Self::Event),\n    ) -> Self::Api<'a> {\n        Api { state, ctx, props, send }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n"
}

  "content": "### 1.8 Connect / API\n\n```rust\n#[derive(ComponentPart)]\n#[scope = \"color-picker\"]\npub enum Part {\n    Root,\n    Label,\n    Control,\n    Trigger,\n    Content,\n    Area,\n    AreaThumb,\n    /// A channel slider container, parameterized by channel.\n    ChannelSlider { channel: ColorChannel },\n    /// A channel slider thumb, parameterized by channel.\n    ChannelSliderThumb { channel: ColorChannel },\n    AlphaSlider,\n    SwatchGroup,\n    /// A preset swatch button. the\n    /// same pattern as `color_swatch_picker::Part::Item`.\n    Swatch { index: usize },\n    FormatSelect,\n    /// A channel text input, parameterized by channel and display index.\n    ChannelInput { channel: ColorChannel, index: usize },\n    HexInput,\n    EyeDropperTrigger,\n    HiddenInput,\n}\n\n/// The connect API for the `ColorPicker` component.\npub struct Api<'a> {\n    state: &'a State,\n    ctx: &'a Context,\n    props: &'a Props,\n    send: &'a dyn Fn(Event),\n}\n\nimpl Api<'_> {\n    // --- Computed state ---\n\n    /// Whether the popover is open.\n    pub const fn is_open(&self) -> bool {\n        !matches!(self.state, State::Closed)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether a thumb is currently being dragged.\n    pub const fn is_dragging(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self.state, State::Dragging { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// The current color value (the pending value, so controlled drags-in-flight\n    /// are reflected).\n    pub fn value(&self) -> &ColorValue {\n        self.ctx.value.pending()\n    }\n\n    /// The current color value formatted as a string in the active format.\n    pub fn value_as_string(&self) -> String {\n        let color color.alpha)\n                } else {\n                    format!(\"rgb({r}, {g}, {b})\")\n                }\n            }\n            ColorFormat::Hsb => {\n                let (h, s, b) = color.to_hsb();\n                format!(\"hsb({h:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)\", s * 100.0, b * 100.0)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The active text format.\n    pub const fn format(&self) -> (self.send)(Event::SetColor(color)); }\n    pub fn set_format(&self, format: ColorFormat) { (self.send)(Event::SetFormat(format)); }\n}\n```\n\nEach `*_attrs` method emits the part's `data-ars-scope`/`data-ars-part` tokens\n(via `Part::data_attrs()`) plus the ARIA/`data-ars-*` attributes and CSS custom\nproperties listed in [§2](#2-anatomy) and [§3](#3-accessibility). Element ids are\nderived on demand from `ctx.ids` — `ids.part(\"trigger\")`, `ids.part(\"content\")`,\n`ids.part(\"area-thumb\")`, `ids.part(\"hue-slider\")`, `ids.part(\"alpha-slider\")`,\n`ids.part(\"label\")`, `ids.part(\"format-select\")`, and `ids.item(\"channel\", &index)`\nfor the channel inputs — rather than precomputed into the context.\n\nHighlights of the part attribute surface:\n\n- **`trigger_attrs`** — `aria-haspopup=\"dialog\"`, `aria-expanded`,\n  `aria-controls` (content id), `aria-labelledby` (label id), and `aria-label`\n  from `messages.trigger_label`; `aria-disabled=\"true\"` + `data-ars-disabled` when\n  disabled.\n- **`content_attrs`** — `role=\"dialog\"`, `aria-labelledby` (label id),\n  `data-ars-state` = `open`/`closed`.\n- **`area_attrs`** — `role=\"group\"` plus the `--ars-color-picker-area-bg` hue\n  backdrop custom property.\n- **`area_thumb_attrs`** — `role=\"application\"`, `aria-roledescription`,\n  `aria-label`, a composed saturation/lightness `aria-valuetext`,\n  `aria-keyshortcuts`, thumb-position custom properties, `tabindex` (`-1` when\n  disabled), and `data-ars-dragging` while dragging.\n- **`channel_slider_attrs(channel)` / `channel_slider_thumb_attrs(channel)`** —\n  `role=\"group\"` / `role=\"slider\"` with `data-ars-channel`, `aria-valuenow`/`min`/\n  `max`, `aria-label`, the thumb-position custom property, and `data-ars-dragging`\n  for the matching channel.\n- **`swatch_attrs(index)`** — `role=\"button\"`, `data-ars-index`, and (when `index`\n  is in range) `aria-label` from `messages.swatch_label`, the `--ars-swatch-color`\n  custom property, and `data-ars-selected` when the swatch equals the current\n  value. /// Whether any context-backed non-`value`/`open` prop changed and the context
/// needs refreshing via [`Event::SetProps`].
fn context_relevant_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {
    old.disabled != new.disabled
        || old.readonly != new.readonly
        || old.close_on_interact_outside != new.close_on_interact_outside
        || old.close_on_escape != new.close_on_escape
        || old.show_alpha != new.show_alpha
        || old.color_space != new.color_space
        || old.swatches != new.swatches
        || old.dir != new.dir
        || old.positioning != new.positioning
        || (old.channel_step - new.channel_step).abs() > f64::EPSILON
        || (old.channel_large_step - new.channel_large_step).abs() > f64::EPSILON
}

// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // user would, so the lifecycle effects fire identically.
        if let (was, Some(now)) = (old.open, new.open)
            && was != Some(now)
        {
            events.push(if now { Event::Open } else { Event::Close });
        }

    /// Select the preset swatch at `index` (click / Enter / Space).
    pub fn on_swatch_click(&self, index: usize) {
        if let Some(color) = self.ctx.swatches.get(index) {
            (self.send)(Event::SetColor(*color));
        }
    }

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve runtime color-space changes across prop syncs**

When a user switches the picker via `Event::ChangeColorSpace`, any later unrelated prop update that triggers `SetProps` (for example changing `swatches`, `dir`, `disabled`, or positioning) will execute this unconditional assignment and reset `ctx.color_space` back to the original prop value. That makes runtime color-space selection fragile and causes the UI to jump back to the initial space even though the color-space prop itself did not change; update this field only when `old.color_space != new.color_space` or separate the initial/default prop from runtime state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GJcbs
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:681
parent_dbid: 3334857518
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow controlled open sync while disabled**

Because `on_props_changed` represents a controlled `open` prop change as `Event::Open`/`Event::Close`, this disabled guard drops parent-driven open synchronization for disabled pickers. For example, a picker mounted with `disabled: true, open: Some(true)` stays `State::Open` when the parent updates `open` to `Some(false)`, leaving the controlled prop unable to close or reopen the component until disabled is cleared; let controlled open sync events through this guard or use a dedicated sync event.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GJcbw
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:689
parent_dbid: 3334857523
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Close explicitly from the dragging state**

`State::Dragging` is still an open popover state, but explicit close requests only match `State::Open`, so a parent-controlled `open: Some(false)` update, `Api::close()`, or Escape-close routed while a drag is active is ignored and the picker remains stuck in `Dragging` with close lifecycle effects such as `DetachClickOutside` never emitted. Keep suppressing interact-outside during pointer capture, but handle explicit close events from `Dragging` as a normal close.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GJcby
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1229
parent_dbid: 3334857526
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent the trigger button from submitting forms**

When the trigger attrs are applied to a real `<button>` inside a form, omitting `type="button"` leaves the HTML default submit behavior in place, so clicking the color-picker trigger can submit the form instead of only toggling the popover. The sibling popover trigger sets `HtmlAttr::Type` to `button`; this trigger should do the same before wiring `aria-haspopup`/toggle behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GJcb4
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1406
parent_dbid: 3334857530
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove disabled channel thumbs from tab order**

With `props.disabled = true`, the area thumb is removed from the tab order, but each channel slider thumb still emits `tabindex="0"` and no disabled state. Disabled pickers therefore expose focusable slider controls whose keyboard events are dropped by the machine, which is confusing for keyboard and assistive-technology users; mirror the disabled handling used by the area thumb here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    #[test]\n    fn disabled_picker_ignores_user_interaction_but_tracks_focus() {\n        let mut svc = service(Props {\n            disabled: true,\n            ..Props::default()\n        });\n\n        // User-initiated toggle is ignored while disabled.\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Toggle));\n        assert_eq!(\n            svc.state(),\n            &State::Closed,\n            \"disabled picker ignores a user toggle\"\n        );\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Focus { part: \"trigger\" }));\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().focused_part, Some(\"trigger\"));\n\n        let trigger = svc.connect(&|_| {}).trigger_attrs();\n        assert_eq!(\n            trigger.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled)),\n            Some(\"true\")\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn disabled_picker_still_honors_controlled_open_sync() {\n        // A controlled, disabled picker must reflect parent-driven open changes\n        // (which arrive as `Open`/`Close`) even though user interaction is\n        // blocked — otherwise it would be stuck until re-enabled.\n        let mut svc = service(Props {\n            disabled: true,\n            open: Some(true),\n            ..Props::default()\n        });\n        assert_eq!(svc.state(), &State::Open);\n\n        drop(svc.set_props(Props {\n            id: \"color-picker\".to_string(),\n            disabled: true,\n            open: Some(false),\n            ..Props::default()\n        }));\n        assert_eq!(svc.state(), &State::Closed);\n\n        drop(svc.set_props(Props {\n            id: \"color-picker\".to_string(),\n            disabled: true,\n            open: Some(true),\n            ..Props::default()\n        }));\n        assert_eq!(svc.state(), &State::Open);\n    }"

Controlled `open` changes arrive as\n        // `Open`/`Close`, so those pass through too — otherwise a disabled,\n        // controlled picker could never be opened/closed by its parent.\n        if ctx.disabled {\n            match event {\n                Event::Open | Event::Close\n                | Event::Focus { .. } | Event::Blur { .. }\n                | Event::SyncValue(_) | Event::SetProps => {}\n                _ => return None,\n            }\n        }\n\n        match (state, event) {\n            (State::Closed, Event::Open | Event::Toggle) => Some(open_plan()),\n\n            // An explicit close is honored from `Dragging` too (parent-controlled\n            // `open: false`, `Api::close()`, `Toggle`, Escape): abandon the drag\n            // and close rather than get stuck open. > AGENT

I've addressed all 5 Codex findings and am waiting on the coverage gate before pushing. Summary of the fixes in flight:

1. **Runtime color-space preservation** — `color_space` is now driven by `ChangeColorSpace` (a prop change routes through it in `on_props_changed`) and removed from the blanket `SetProps` sync, so an unrelated prop update no longer reverts a runtime switch.
2. **Controlled open sync while disabled** — the disabled guard now lets `Open`/`Close` through (only user `Toggle`/interaction is ignored).
3. **Close from `Dragging`** — `Close`/`Toggle`/`CloseOnEscape` now resolve from `Dragging` (abandoning the drag), while interact-outside stays suppressed during pointer capture.
4. **Trigger `type="button"`** — prevents form submission.
5. **Disabled channel thumbs + swatches** — now `tabindex="-1"` + `aria-disabled` like the area thumb.

Each has a new test (TDD), two existing disabled-semantics tests were updated, the 3 trigger snapshots re-accepted (only `type="button"` added), and the spec §1.7/§1.8/§2/§3.1 synced. Tests (85), clippy `-D warnings`, and the insta orphan check are all green; spec validates and snippets compile.

Once `cargo xcov` confirms the branch threshold holds, I'll commit, push, reply+resolve each Codex thread, and re-trigger `@codex review` — looping until 👍.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let drags terminate after disabling**

If a parent disables the picker while the user is dragging, `SetProps` can put the context in `disabled = true` while the state remains `Dragging`; the subsequent pointer-up `DragEnd` is then rejected by this guard, so the machine stays in `Dragging` and never fires `on_change_end` or clears `data-ars-dragging`. The sibling `ColorArea` explicitly allows `DragEnd` through this disabled guard for the same mid-drag-disable scenario, so this component should do the same.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remap controls when color space changes**

For `Event::ChangeColorSpace`, this only updates `ctx.color_space`, but the actual editable controls still hard-code the area to saturation/lightness and the non-alpha slider to hue. When `Props::color_space` starts as or changes to `Rgb`/`Hsb`, `Context::channels()` advertises a different channel set, yet area drags/keyboard and slider labels continue editing HSL channels, so the visible controls do not match the selected color space.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GJ-BS
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:537  parent_dbid: 3335042510
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve hue endpoint on channel drags**

When the hue slider is dragged to `x == 1.0` or set to its max via keyboard, this sends `360` through `with_channel`, which constructs a `ColorValue` whose hue is wrapped into `[0, 360)`. The value immediately becomes `0`, so the thumb position and `aria-valuenow` jump back to the start instead of staying at the right-hand 360° endpoint; the standalone `ColorSlider` keeps an unwrapped slider value specifically to avoid this endpoint collapse.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark the disabled area thumb for assistive tech**

In the disabled picker case, the area thumb only leaves the tab order; unlike the channel thumbs and swatches, it never receives `aria-disabled="true"`. Because this custom `role="application"` control is still present in the accessibility tree, screen-reader users can encounter it without any disabled state even though the machine drops its editing events.

`channels()` is documented as the adapter source for laying out per-channel inputs, but every returned slice omits `ColorChannel::Alpha` even though `show_alpha` defaults to true and the props promise an alpha slider and input. An adapter that follows this API will render RGB/HSL/HSB inputs but never render the alpha input, leaving translucent colors impossible to edit numerically.

=== §1.6 (says remap) ===
### 1.6 Color Space Switching

`ColorPicker` supports runtime color space switching via `Event::ChangeColorSpace(ColorSpace)`.

**Transition Behavior** for `ChangeColorSpace(new_space)`:

1. **Recompute value**: Convert the current color value from the old color space to `new_space`. Preserve perceptual magnitudes where possible (e.g., HSL->HSB preserves hue and saturation, converts lightness to brightness).
2. **Update context**: Set `ctx.color_space = new_space`. Update `ctx.value` with the converted color.
3. **Remap channels**: The color area and channel sliders update to reflect the new space's channels (e.g., switching from RGB to HSL changes the area from Red/Green to Hue/Saturation, and the slider from Blue to Lightness).
4. **Live region announcement**: Emit an `aria-live="polite"` announcement: `"Switched to {space} color space"` (e.g., "Switched to HSL color space"). This informs screen reader users that the control layout has changed.

**UI Affordance**: The color space selector (button group, dropdown, or segmented control) emits `Event::ChangeColorSpace(selected_space)` when the user selects a different space. The spec does not prescribe a specific UI pattern -- adapters choose the appropriate control.
=== DragTarget::Area (says fixed) ===

=== anatomy Area description ===
1451:│   ├── Area                    (required — 2D saturation/lightness gradient)

> AGENT

The user wants the tradeoffs and the clear winner. Here's my analysis:

**Option 2 (full per-space remap)** is the one §1.6's example literally describes — but no real picker implements it. RGB has no perceptually-navigable 2D "hue square," so a "red×green area with a blue slider" is meaningless to users; Ark UI and React Aria both render RGB as plain channel sliders/inputs, never a 2D area. It's the most work *and* a worse UX. Reject.

**Option 1 (always saturation×lightness)** is simplest and matches the `DragTarget`/anatomy text, but it's subtly wrong in HSB mode: the visual square stays sat×*lightness* while the numeric inputs show *brightness*, so the picker isn't truly HSB-correct despite advertising first-class HSB support.

**Option 3 (area = saturation × {lightness for HSL/RGB/HEX, brightness for HSB}; hue+alpha sliders fixed; color_space drives the numeric inputs)** is exactly how real pickers behave — the 2D square reflects the chosen cylindrical space's S and L/V axes (the classic HSV square vs HSL square), hue/alpha are always hue/alpha, and RGB/HEX reuse the HSL square as the visual picker since they have no hue square. It's bounded (parametrize one axis), HSB-correct, and lets me reconcile §1.6 to a coherent contract instead of its nonsensical RGB example.

**Clear winner: Option 3.** It's the best-outcome design without Option 2's invented RGB area. I'll implement it plus the 7 bug fixes. Let me track this batch and start.

  "new_string": "impl Context {\n    /// Returns the channels available in the current color space, in display\n    /// order. Used by adapters to lay out the per-channel inputs.\n    ///\n    /// `Alpha` is appended whenever [`show_alpha`](Self::show_alpha) is set, so an\n    /// adapter that renders one input per returned channel also renders the alpha\n    /// input the `show_alpha`/alpha-slider contract promises. (HWB maps onto the\n    /// HSL channel triplet for the numeric inputs.)\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn channels(&self) -> &'static [ColorChannel] {\n        match (self.color_space, self.show_alpha) {\n            (ColorSpace::Rgb, false) => {\n                &[ColorChannel::Red, ColorChannel::Green, ColorChannel::Blue]\n            }\n            (ColorSpace::Rgb, true) => &[\n                ColorChannel::Red,\n                ColorChannel::Green,\n                ColorChannel::Blue,\n                ColorChannel::Alpha,\n            ],\n            (ColorSpace::Hsl | ColorSpace::Hwb, false) => &[\n                ColorChannel::Hue,\n                ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                ColorChannel::Lightness,\n            ],\n            (ColorSpace::Hsl | ColorSpace::Hwb, true) => &[\n                ColorChannel::Hue,\n                ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                ColorChannel::Lightness,\n                ColorChannel::Alpha,\n            ],\n            (ColorSpace::Hsb, false) => &[\n                ColorChannel::Hue,\n                ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                ColorChannel::Brightness,\n            ],\n            (ColorSpace::Hsb, true) => &[\n                ColorChannel::Hue,\n                ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                ColorChannel::Brightness,\n                ColorChannel::Alpha,\n            ],\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The vertical channel the 2D area edits in the current color space:\n    /// brightness for HSB, lightness for HSL / RGB / HEX. (The horizontal axis is\n    /// always saturation; the hue and alpha sliders are space-independent.)\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn area_y_channel(&self) -> ColorChannel {\n        match self.color_space {\n            ColorSpace::Hsb => ColorChannel::Brightness,\n            _ => ColorChannel::Lightness,\n        }\n    }\n}"

567	/// Both base the new color on the *pending* value so a controlled drag-in-flight
568	/// accumulates rather than re-reading the stale controlled prop.
569	fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {
570	    let current = *ctx.value.pending();
571	
572	    match target {
573	        DragTarget::Area => {
574	            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
575	            let lightness = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
576	
577	            ctx.value.set(ColorValue::new(
578	                current.hue,
579	                saturation,
580	                lightness,
581	                current.alpha,
582	            ));
583	        }
584	
585	        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {
586	            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);
587	            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);
588	
589	            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&current, channel, value));
590	        }
591	    }
592	}

  "new_string": "fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => {\n            let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let y_value = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            // The area's vertical axis is brightness in HSB, lightness otherwise.\n            let y_channel = ctx.area_y_channel();\n            let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);\n            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, y_channel, y_value));\n        }\n\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Set a single channel on the pending color, keeping the unwrapped\n/// [`Context::hue_value`] in sync when the hue channel is edited so the 360°\n/// endpoint survives [`ColorValue`]'s `[0, 360)` hue wrap.\nfn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {\n    let base = *ctx.value.pending();\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {\n        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-derive the cached unwrapped hue from the current color after an external\n/// full-color set (text input, swatch, eyedropper, controlled-value sync).\nfn sync_hue_from_color(ctx: &mut Context) {\n    ctx.hue_value = ctx.value.pending().hue;\n}"
}

973	        // The id is baked into Context::ids (and every aria-* relationship that
974	        // points at it) at init; allowing it to change would silently break the

In\n    /// RTL the saturation (x-axis) arrows are mirrored.\n    pub fn on_area_thumb_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData, shift: bool) {\n        let saturation_step = self.keyboard_step(ColorChannel::Saturation, shift);\n        let lightness_step = self.keyboard_step(ColorChannel::Lightness, shift);\n\n        let rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;\n\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => (self.send)(if rtl {\n                Event::ChannelDecrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            } else {\n                Event::ChannelIncrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => (self.send)(if rtl {\n                Event::ChannelIncrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            } else {\n                Event::ChannelDecrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::ChannelIncrement {\n                channel: ColorChannel::Lightness,\n                step: lightness_step,\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::ChannelDecrement {\n                channel: ColorChannel::Lightness,\n                step: lightness_step,\n            }),",
  "new_string": "    /// Handle arrow/Home/End keydown on the area thumb. Left/Right adjust\n    /// saturation, Up/Down adjust the area's vertical channel (brightness in HSB,\n    /// lightness otherwise); `shift` selects the large step. In RTL the saturation\n    /// (x-axis) arrows are mirrored.\n    pub fn on_area_thumb_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData, shift: bool) {\n        let saturation_step = self.keyboard_step(ColorChannel::Saturation, shift);\n        let y_channel = self.ctx.area_y_channel();\n        let y_step = self.keyboard_step(y_channel, shift);\n\n        let rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;\n\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => (self.send)(if rtl {\n                Event::ChannelDecrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            } else {\n                Event::ChannelIncrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => (self.send)(if rtl {\n                Event::ChannelIncrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            } else {\n                Event::ChannelDecrement {\n                    channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n                    step: saturation_step,\n                }\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::ChannelIncrement {\n                channel: y_channel,\n                step: y_step,\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::ChannelDecrement {\n                channel: y_channel,\n                step: y_step,\n            }),"
}

895	
896	`ColorPicker` supports runtime color space switching via `Event::ChangeColorSpace(ColorSpace)`.
897	
898	**Transition Behavior** for `ChangeColorSpace(new_space)`:
899	
900	1. **Recompute value**: Convert the current color value from the old color space to `new_space`. Preserve perceptual magnitudes where possible (e.g., HSL->HSB preserves hue and saturation, converts lightness to brightness).
901	2. **Update context**: Set `ctx.color_space = new_space`. Update `ctx.value` with the converted color.
902	3. **Remap channels**: The color area and channel sliders update to reflect the new space's channels (e.g., switching from RGB to HSL changes the area from Red/Green to Hue/Saturation, and the slider from Blue to Lightness).
903	4. **Live region announcement**: Emit an `aria-live="polite"` announcement: `"Switched to {space} color space"` (e.g., "Switched to HSL color space"). This informs screen reader users that the control layout has changed.
904	
905	**UI Affordance**: The color space selector (button group, dropdown, or segmented control) emits `Event::ChangeColorSpace(selected_space)` when the user selects a different space. The spec does not prescribe a specific UI pattern -- adapters choose the appropriate control.
906	
907	**Supported Spaces**: All spaces in the `ColorSpace` enum (RGB, HSL, HSB/HSV, HEX) are switchable at runtime. The conversion between spaces is lossless for the sRGB gamut (minor floating-point rounding is acceptable).
908

  "new_string": "**Transition Behavior** for `ChangeColorSpace(new_space)`:\n\n1. **Update context**: Set `ctx.color_space = new_space`. The stored `ColorValue` is unchanged — the same color is simply presented through the new space's parameters.\n2. **Remap the numeric inputs**: `Context::channels()` returns the new space's channel set (RGB→`[R, G, B]`, HSL→`[H, S, L]`, HSB→`[H, S, B]`, plus `Alpha` when `show_alpha`), so the per-channel text inputs re-label and re-bind to the new channels.\n3. **Remap the 2D area's vertical axis**: the area is always the visual saturation × {lightness | brightness} square of the current hue — `Context::area_y_channel()` returns brightness in HSB and lightness in HSL/RGB/HEX. The horizontal axis is always saturation, and the hue and alpha sliders are space-independent (always hue/alpha). The area is **not** remapped to arbitrary channel pairs: RGB/HEX have no perceptually-navigable hue square (they are edited through the numeric inputs), so they reuse the HSL square as the visual picker. This is the standard Ark UI / React Aria picker model.\n4. **Live region announcement**: Emit an `aria-live=\"polite\"` announcement: `\"Switched to {space} color space\"` (e.g., \"Switched to HSL color space\"). This informs screen reader users that the control layout has changed.\n\nA controlled `color_space` prop change is routed through this same `Event::ChangeColorSpace` from `on_props_changed`, so a prop-driven switch announces and remaps identically to a runtime one — and `SetProps` never touches `color_space`, so an unrelated prop update cannot revert a runtime switch.\n\n**UI Affordance**: The color space selector (button group, dropdown, or segmented control) emits `Event::ChangeColorSpace(selected_space)` when the user selects a different space. The spec does not prescribe a specific UI pattern -- adapters choose the appropriate control."

948	
949	/// Apply an adapter-normalized pointer position to the color value for the given
950	/// drag target. `Area` maps x→saturation `[0, 1]` and y→lightness `[1, 0]`
951	/// (top = lightest); `Channel` maps x across the channel's full range. Both base
952	/// the new color on the *pending* value so a controlled drag-in-flight
953	/// accumulates rather than re-reading the stale controlled prop.
954	fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {
955	    let current = *ctx.value.pending();
956	    match target {
957	        DragTarget::Area => {
958	            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
959	            let lightness = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
960	            ctx.value.set(ColorValue::new(current.hue, saturation, lightness, current.alpha));
961	        }
962	        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {
963	            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);
964	            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);
965	            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&current, channel, value));
966	        }
967	    }
968	}
969	
970	/// Invoke `Props::on_change_end` with the pending (drag-staged) color.
971	fn change_end_effect() -> PendingEffect<Machine> {
972	    PendingEffect::new(Effect::ChangeEnd, |ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {
973	        if let Some(callback) = &props.on_change_end {
974	            callback(*ctx.value.pending());
975	        }
976	        no_cleanup()
977	    })
978	}

981	/// (`Closed → Open`) and `Machine::initial_effects` (booted-open) so the two
982	/// entry points stay in lock-step.
983	fn open_lifecycle_effects() -> [PendingEffect<Machine>; 2] {
984	    [
985	        PendingEffect::named(Effect::AttachClickOutside),
986	        PendingEffect::named(Effect::DetectEyedropper),
987	    ]
988	}

990	fn open_plan() -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {
991	    let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Open).apply(|ctx: &mut Context| ctx.open.set(true));
992	    for effect in open_lifecycle_effects() {
993	        plan = plan.with_effect(effect);
994	    }

1005	fn context_relevant_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {
1006	    old.disabled != new.disabled

1008	        || old.close_on_interact_outside != new.close_on_interact_outside

  "old_string": "/// Apply an adapter-normalized pointer position to the color value for the given\n/// drag target. `Area` maps x→saturation `[0, 1]` and y→lightness `[1, 0]`\n/// (top = lightest); `Channel` maps x across the channel's full range. Both base\n/// the new color on the *pending* value so a controlled drag-in-flight\n/// accumulates rather than re-reading the stale controlled prop.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => {\n            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let lightness = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            ctx.value.set(ColorValue::new(current.hue, saturation, lightness, current.alpha));\n        }\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&current, channel, value));\n        }\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Apply an adapter-normalized pointer position to the color value for the given\n/// drag target. `Area` maps x→saturation `[0, 1]` and y→the area's vertical\n/// channel `[1, 0]` (brightness in HSB, lightness otherwise); `Channel` maps x\n/// across the channel's full range. Bases the new color on the *pending* value\n/// so a controlled drag-in-flight accumulates.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => {\n            let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let y_value = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let y_channel = ctx.area_y_channel(); // brightness in HSB, else lightness\n            let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);\n            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, y_channel, y_value));\n        }\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Set one channel, keeping the unwrapped `hue_value` in sync when hue is edited\n/// so the 360° endpoint survives `ColorValue`'s `[0, 360)` hue wrap.\nfn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {\n    let base = *ctx.value.pending();\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {\n        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-derive the cached unwrapped hue after an external full-color set.\nfn sync_hue_from_color(ctx: &mut Context) { ctx.hue_value = ctx.value.pending().hue; }\n\n/// The current value of `channel` for keyboard stepping — the unwrapped\n/// `hue_value` for hue, the live color value otherwise.\nfn channel_current(ctx: &Context, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue { ctx.hue_value } else { channel_value(ctx.value.pending(), channel) }\n}"
}

1366	                format!("hsb({h:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)", s * 100.0, b * 100.0)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow disabled prop sync to change color space**

When a disabled picker receives a `set_props` where only `color_space` changes, `on_props_changed` enqueues `Event::ChangeColorSpace`, but this disabled-event gate drops it before the `ChangeColorSpace` arm can update `ctx.color_space`. Because `Service::set_props` has already replaced the stored props and `SetProps` intentionally excludes `color_space`, a disabled component can remain permanently stuck with the old channel set even after the parent has switched the prop.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark the eyedropper trigger as a non-submit button**

If an adapter renders the eyedropper trigger as a real `<button>` inside a form, these attrs do not provide `type="button"`, so the HTML default is submit. The trigger and swatch attrs already guard this case; without the same attr here, clicking the eyedropper in a form can submit/navigate instead of just opening the browser picker.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Only mark the area thumb while the area is dragged**

During a hue or alpha slider drag the state is still `Dragging`, so `self.is_dragging()` makes the area thumb get `data-ars-dragging` even though the active target is `DragTarget::Channel(_)`. Any styling or adapter logic keyed off this part-level flag will show the area thumb as active while another thumb is being dragged; this should check for `DragTarget::Area` like the channel thumb path checks for its own channel.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve alpha when formatting HSB values**

When the current color is translucent and the active format is `ColorFormat::Hsb`, `value_as_string()` always emits `hsb(...)` without the alpha component. That makes the visible HSB text disagree with the canonical formatter, which emits `hsba(...)`, and an adapter/user round-trip through this string will silently turn the color opaque.

The channel text input attrs expose type/input mode and channel metadata but never set `HtmlAttr::Value`. In adapters that use the connect API attrs as the source of input props, the RGB/HSL/HSB channel inputs render blank or stale instead of showing the current channel value, so users cannot see the existing color before editing unless each adapter reimplements the formatting itself.

573	///
574	/// For [`DragTarget::Area`] the x-axis maps to saturation `[0, 1]` and the
575	/// y-axis maps to lightness `[1, 0]` (top = lightest). For
576	/// [`DragTarget::Channel`] the x-axis maps across the channel's full range.
577	/// Both base the new color on the *pending* value so a controlled drag-in-flight
578	/// accumulates rather than re-reading the stale controlled prop.
579	fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {
580	    match target {
581	        DragTarget::Area => {
582	            let current = *ctx.value.pending();
583	            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
584	            let y_value = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
585	            // The area's vertical axis is brightness in HSB, lightness otherwise.
586	            let y_channel = ctx.area_y_channel();
587	            let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);
588	            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, y_channel, y_value));
589	        }
590	
591	        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {
592	            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);
593	            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);
594	            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);
595	        }
596	    }
597	}
598	
599	/// Set a single channel on the pending color, keeping the unwrapped
600	/// [`Context::hue_value`] in sync when the hue channel is edited so the 360°
601	/// endpoint survives [`ColorValue`]'s `[0, 360)` hue wrap.
602	fn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {
603	    let base = *ctx.value.pending();
604	    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));
605	    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {
606	        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);
607	    }
608	}

  "old_string": "/// For [`DragTarget::Area`] the x-axis maps to saturation `[0, 1]` and the\n/// y-axis maps to lightness `[1, 0]` (top = lightest). For\n/// [`DragTarget::Channel`] the x-axis maps across the channel's full range.\n/// Both base the new color on the *pending* value so a controlled drag-in-flight\n/// accumulates rather than re-reading the stale controlled prop.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => {\n            let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let y_value = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            // The area's vertical axis is brightness in HSB, lightness otherwise.\n            let y_channel = ctx.area_y_channel();\n            let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);\n            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, y_channel, y_value));\n        }\n\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);\n        }\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// For [`DragTarget::Area`] the x-axis maps to saturation `[0, 1]` and the\n/// y-axis maps to the area's vertical channel `[1, 0]` (top = max), interpreted\n/// in the active color space (HSB saturation × brightness for HSB, HSL\n/// saturation × lightness otherwise). For [`DragTarget::Channel`] the x-axis maps\n/// across the channel's full range. Both base the new color on the *pending*\n/// value so a controlled drag-in-flight accumulates rather than re-reading the\n/// stale controlled prop.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => set_area(ctx, x, 1.0 - y),\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The current area coordinates `(saturation, y)` in `0..=1`, interpreted in the\n/// active color space: HSB saturation × brightness for HSB, HSL saturation ×\n/// lightness otherwise.\nfn area_axes(ctx: &Context) -> (f64, f64) {\n    let color = ctx.value.pending();\n    if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {\n        let (_, hsb_saturation, brightness) = color.to_hsb();\n        (hsb_saturation, brightness)\n    } else {\n        (color.saturation, color.lightness)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Write the area coordinates `(saturation, y)` back to the pending color,\n/// space-aware so HSB edits stay coherent in HSB space (both axes set together\n/// via [`ColorValue::from_hsb`]) rather than mixing HSL saturation with HSB\n/// brightness. Hue and alpha are preserved.\nfn set_area(ctx: &mut Context, saturation: f64, y: f64) {\n    let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n    let saturation = saturation.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    let y = y.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n\n    let next = if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {\n        let mut color = ColorValue::from_hsb(current.hue, saturation, y);\n        color.alpha = current.alpha;\n        color\n    } else {\n        let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);\n        with_channel(&updated, ColorChannel::Lightness, y)\n    };\n\n    ctx.value.set(next);\n}"
}

  "new_string": "    pub fn on_area_thumb_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData, shift: bool) {\n        // Both area axes are fractional `[0, 1]`, so they share the saturation\n        // step (1% default, 10% with Shift). The area emits its own `AreaXStep`/\n        // `AreaYStep` so the machine can apply them space-aware (HSB vs HSL).\n        let step = self.keyboard_step(ColorChannel::Saturation, shift);\n        let rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;\n\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => {\n                (self.send)(Event::AreaXStep(if rtl { -step } else { step }));\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {\n                (self.send)(Event::AreaXStep(if rtl { step } else { -step }));\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::AreaYStep(step)),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::AreaYStep(-step)),\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }"
}

{

  "file_path": "/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-300/crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs",
  "old_string": "/// Set a single channel on the pending color, keeping the unwrapped\n/// [`Context::hue_value`] in sync when the hue channel is edited so the 360°\n/// endpoint survives [`ColorValue`]'s `[0, 360)` hue wrap.\nfn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {\n    let base = *ctx.value.pending();\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {\n        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-derive the cached unwrapped hue from the current color after an external\n/// full-color set (text input, swatch, eyedropper, controlled-value sync).\nconst fn sync_hue_from_color(ctx: &mut Context) {\n    ctx.hue_value = ctx.value.pending().hue;\n}\n\n/// The current value of `channel` for keyboard stepping — the unwrapped\n/// [`Context::hue_value`] for hue (so stepping near the 360° endpoint does not\n/// collapse to 0°), the live color value otherwise.\nfn channel_current(ctx: &Context, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {\n        ctx.hue_value\n    } else {\n        channel_value(ctx.value.pending(), channel)\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Set a single channel on the pending color, space-aware so the value the user\n/// edits matches the active color space:\n///\n/// - **Hue** also updates the unwrapped [`Context::hue_value`] so the 360°\n///   endpoint survives [`ColorValue`]'s `[0, 360)` wrap.\n/// - **Saturation in HSB** is HSB saturation (set via [`ColorValue::from_hsb`]\n///   keeping the current brightness), so the numeric S input stays consistent\n///   with the HSB area; in every other space it is HSL saturation.\n/// - All other channels go straight through [`with_channel`].\nfn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {\n    let base = *ctx.value.pending();\n\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Saturation && ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {\n        let (hue, _, brightness) = base.to_hsb();\n        let mut next = ColorValue::from_hsb(hue, value, brightness);\n        next.alpha = base.alpha;\n        ctx.value.set(next);\n        return;\n    }\n\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {\n        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-derive the cached unwrapped hue from the current color after an external\n/// full-color set (text input, swatch, eyedropper, controlled-value sync).\nconst fn sync_hue_from_color(ctx: &mut Context) {\n    ctx.hue_value = ctx.value.pending().hue;\n}\n\n/// The current value of `channel` for keyboard stepping and numeric display,\n/// space-aware to mirror [`set_channel_value`]: the unwrapped\n/// [`Context::hue_value`] for hue, HSB saturation for Saturation in HSB, the\n/// live color value otherwise.\nfn channel_current(ctx: &Context, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {\n    match channel {\n        ColorChannel::Hue => ctx.hue_value,\n        ColorChannel::Saturation if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb => {\n            ctx.value.pending().to_hsb().1\n        }\n        _ => channel_value(ctx.value.pending(), channel),\n    }\n}"
}

968	/// Apply an adapter-normalized pointer position to the color value for the given
969	/// drag target. `Area` maps x→saturation `[0, 1]` and y→the area's vertical
970	/// channel `[1, 0]` (brightness in HSB, lightness otherwise); `Channel` maps x
971	/// across the channel's full range. Bases the new color on the *pending* value
972	/// so a controlled drag-in-flight accumulates.
973	fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {
974	    match target {
975	        DragTarget::Area => {
976	            let current = *ctx.value.pending();
977	            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
978	            let y_value = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
979	            let y_channel = ctx.area_y_channel(); // brightness in HSB, else lightness
980	            let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);
981	            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, y_channel, y_value));
982	        }
983	        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {
984	            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);
985	            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);
986	            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);
987	        }
988	    }
989	}

991	/// Set one channel, keeping the unwrapped `hue_value` in sync when hue is edited
992	/// so the 360° endpoint survives `ColorValue`'s `[0, 360)` hue wrap.
993	fn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {
994	    let base = *ctx.value.pending();
995	    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));
996	    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {
997	        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);
998	    }
999	}

  "old_string": "fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => {\n            let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n            let saturation = x.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let y_value = (1.0 - y).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let y_channel = ctx.area_y_channel(); // brightness in HSB, else lightness\n            let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);\n            ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, y_channel, y_value));\n        }\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Set one channel, keeping the unwrapped `hue_value` in sync when hue is edited\n/// so the 360° endpoint survives `ColorValue`'s `[0, 360)` hue wrap.\nfn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {\n    let base = *ctx.value.pending();\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {\n        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-derive the cached unwrapped hue after an external full-color set.\nfn sync_hue_from_color(ctx: &mut Context) { ctx.hue_value = ctx.value.pending().hue; }\n\n/// The current value of `channel` for keyboard stepping — the unwrapped\n/// `hue_value` for hue, the live color value otherwise.\nfn channel_current(ctx: &Context, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue { ctx.hue_value } else { channel_value(ctx.value.pending(), channel) }\n}",
  "new_string": "fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => set_area(ctx, x, 1.0 - y),\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Current area coordinates `(saturation, y)` in `0..=1`, interpreted in the\n/// active space: HSB saturation × brightness for HSB, HSL saturation × lightness\n/// otherwise.\nfn area_axes(ctx: &Context) -> (f64, f64) {\n    let color = ctx.value.pending();\n    if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {\n        let (_, s, v) = color.to_hsb();\n        (s, v)\n    } else {\n        (color.saturation, color.lightness)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Write the area coordinates back to the pending color, space-aware so HSB edits\n/// set both axes together via `from_hsb` (no HSL-sat/HSB-bright mixing). Hue/alpha\n/// preserved.\nfn set_area(ctx: &mut Context, saturation: f64, y: f64) {\n    let current = *ctx.value.pending();\n    let s = saturation.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    let y = y.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    let next = if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {\n        let mut color = ColorValue::from_hsb(current.hue, s, y);\n        color.alpha = current.alpha;\n        color\n    } else {\n        let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, s);\n        with_channel(&updated, ColorChannel::Lightness, y)\n    };\n    ctx.value.set(next);\n}\n\n/// Set one channel, space-aware: hue also updates the unwrapped `hue_value` (360°\n/// endpoint), Saturation-in-HSB is HSB saturation (via `from_hsb`, preserving\n/// brightness) so the numeric S input matches the HSB area, others go through\n/// `with_channel`.\nfn set_channel_value(ctx: &mut Context, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) {\n    let base = *ctx.value.pending();\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Saturation && ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {\n        let (hue, _, brightness) = base.to_hsb();\n        let mut next = ColorValue::from_hsb(hue, value, brightness);\n        next.alpha = base.alpha;\n        ctx.value.set(next);\n        return;\n    }\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));\n    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {\n        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-derive the cached unwrapped hue after an external full-color set.\nfn sync_hue_from_color(ctx: &mut Context) { ctx.hue_value = ctx.value.pending().hue; }\n\n/// Current value of `channel` for keyboard stepping / numeric display — unwrapped\n/// `hue_value` for hue, HSB saturation for Saturation-in-HSB, live value otherwise.\nfn channel_current(ctx: &Context, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {\n    match channel {\n        ColorChannel::Hue => ctx.hue_value,\n        ColorChannel::Saturation if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb => {\n            ctx.value.pending().to_hsb().1\n        }\n        _ => channel_value(ctx.value.pending(), channel),\n    }\n}"
}

  "new_string": "        assert!((channel_value(&dimmed, ColorChannel::Brightness) - 0.5).abs() < 0.02);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn from_hsb_round_trips_with_to_hsb() {\n        // A spread of HSB triplets must survive from_hsb -> to_hsb intact.\n        for &(h, s, v) in &[\n            (0.0, 1.0, 1.0),    // pure red\n            (210.0, 0.5, 0.4),  // muted blue\n            (120.0, 0.8, 0.7),  // green\n            (0.0, 0.0, 0.0),    // black (saturation irrelevant)\n            (0.0, 0.0, 1.0),    // white\n            (300.0, 0.3, 0.9),  // pale magenta\n        ] {\n            let (rh, rs, rv) = ColorValue::from_hsb(h, s, v).to_hsb();\n            assert!((rv - v).abs() < 1e-6, \"brightness {v} -> {rv}\");\n            // Saturation/hue are only meaningful when brightness is non-zero.\n            if v > 0.0 {\n                assert!((rs - s).abs() < 1e-6, \"saturation {s} -> {rs}\");\n                if s > 0.0 {\n                    assert!((rh - h).abs() < 1e-6, \"hue {h} -> {rh}\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Out-of-range inputs are clamped, full alpha by default.\n        let clamped = ColorValue::from_hsb(0.0, 2.0, -1.0);\n        assert!((clamped.alpha - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);\n        assert_eq!(clamped.to_hsb().2, 0.0);\n    }"
}

file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1773
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable the format selector when the picker is disabled**

When `Props.disabled` is true and an adapter renders `FormatSelect` as the documented native `<select>` or a button, this attr map still exposes an enabled, focusable control with no `disabled`, `aria-disabled`, or tab-index suppression, while the machine's disabled guard drops `Event::SetFormat`. That leaves keyboard and AT users able to reach a control that appears operable but cannot change anything; mirror the disabled handling used by the other interactive parts.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GMMw-  parent_dbid: 3335827301
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:821
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass eyedropper support updates while disabled**

When a picker is opened while disabled (for example via controlled `open`/`default_open`), the open lifecycle still emits `DetectEyedropper`, but the adapter's `Event::SetEyedropperSupported(true)` response is filtered out by this disabled guard. If the parent later enables the already-open picker, `ctx.eyedropper_supported` is still false and the eyedropper trigger remains hidden until the picker is closed and reopened; treat this adapter capability report like the other non-user sync events.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GMMxF  parent_dbid: 3335827310
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1783
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose a channel edit dispatcher**

When an adapter renders the per-channel text inputs from `Context::channels()`/`channel_input_attrs`, there is no public `Api` method corresponding to `Event::SetChannel`; the `send` closure is private, and the only generic value action is `set_value(ColorValue)`. That leaves adapters either unable to make these inputs edit their individual channels through the connect API or forced to hand-build machine events, unlike the other interactive parts that have typed dispatch helpers.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GMMxK  parent_dbid: 3335827314
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1389
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate dir onto the root attrs**

When `Props.dir` is `Rtl`, the core mirrors keyboard handling but the connect attrs never expose `dir="rtl"` (or any direction token) on the root. The spec requires the area gradient/layout to flip horizontally in RTL, and existing components expose `HtmlAttr::Dir` for this; without it, styles/adapters driven from the attr map render the visual picker LTR while the arrow keys behave RTL.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GMMxM  parent_dbid: 3335827318
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1349
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Announce color spaces with user-facing labels**

When the default `color_space_switched` message is used, this passes Rust `Debug` names such as `Rgb`, `Hsl`, and `Hsb`, so screen readers hear strings like “Switched to Hsl color space” instead of the spec's user-facing labels such as “HSL”. Map the enum to display labels before invoking the message.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    /// Set the active text format.\n    pub fn set_format(&self, format: ColorFormat) {\n        (self.send)(Event::SetFormat(format));\n    }\n\n    /// Set a single channel from its numeric input, in the same display units\n    /// [`channel_input_attrs`](Self::channel_input_attrs) exposes: degrees for\n    /// hue, raw `0`–`255` for the RGB channels, and a `0`–`100` percentage for the\n    /// fractional channels (saturation, lightness, brightness, alpha). The\n    /// percentage is converted back to the `0..=1` channel unit before dispatch,\n    /// so reading and writing an input round-trip. Space-aware: in HSB, the\n    /// `Saturation` channel is HSB saturation.\n    pub fn set_channel(&self, channel: ColorChannel, display_value: f64) {\n        let value = match channel {\n            ColorChannel::Hue\n            | ColorChannel::Red\n            | ColorChannel::Green\n            | ColorChannel::Blue => display_value,\n            _ => display_value / 100.0,\n        };\n        (self.send)(Event::SetChannel { channel, value });\n    }\n\n    // --- Part attrs ---"
}

  "new_string": "    /// The `aria-live` announcement for the active color space, used by the\n    /// `Effect::AnnounceColorSpace` adapter handler. Uses the user-facing\n    /// upper-case label (`\"RGB\"`, `\"HSL\"`, …) via `color_space_label`, not the\n    /// Rust `Debug` name, so screen readers hear \"Switched to HSL color space\".\n    pub fn color_space_announcement(&self) -> String {\n        (self.ctx.messages.color_space_switched)(color_space_label(self.ctx.color_space), &self.ctx.locale)\n    }\n\n    // --- Imperative actions ---\n\n    pub fn open(&self) { (self.send)(Event::Open); }\n    pub fn close(&self) { (self.send)(Event::Close); }\n    pub fn set_value(&self, color: ColorValue) { (self.send)(Event::SetColor(color)); }\n    pub fn set_format(&self, format: ColorFormat) { (self.send)(Event::SetFormat(format)); }\n\n    /// Set one channel from its numeric input, in the same display units\n    /// `channel_input_attrs` exposes (degrees for hue, `0`–`255` for RGB, a\n    /// `0`–`100` percent for the fractional channels). The percent is converted\n    /// back to the `0..=1` channel unit so reading and writing an input\n    /// round-trip; space-aware (HSB saturation in HSB).\n    pub fn set_channel(&self, channel: ColorChannel, display_value: f64) {\n        let value = match channel {\n            ColorChannel::Hue | ColorChannel::Red | ColorChannel::Green | ColorChannel::Blue => display_value,\n            _ => display_value / 100.0,\n        };\n        (self.send)(Event::SetChannel { channel, value });\n    }\n}\n```\n\n`color_space_label(space)` maps the `ColorSpace` enum to its user-facing\nupper-case label (`Rgb → \"RGB\"`, `Hsl → \"HSL\"`, `Hsb → \"HSB\"`, `Hwb → \"HWB\"`)."
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve fractional alpha in slider ARIA values**

When this thumb is used for the alpha channel, formatting `aria-valuenow` with `{value:.0}` rounds every partially transparent value to `0` or `1` (for example the committed snapshot shows a 50% alpha thumb positioned at `50.0%` but announcing `aria-valuenow="0"`). That makes screen readers report the wrong slider value for any alpha between 0 and 1 even though the visual position and submitted color are correct; use the actual fractional value or percentage consistently with the alpha range.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GM5PY  parent_dbid: 3336076183
