**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Populate the hex input value**

When an adapter renders the optional `HexInput` by spreading this attr map, the text field has no current value, so the picker opens with a blank hex field even though the channel inputs just above expose their current values from the connect API. Since this part is the hex color text input, include the current `to_hex(show_alpha)` value here so adapters do not have to duplicate color formatting outside the agnostic API.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GM5Pc  parent_dbid: 3336076188
file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1075
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync open when switching to controlled mode**

When a picker has been mounted uncontrolled (`old.open == None`) and the parent later starts controlling it with `open: Some(false)` or `Some(true)`, this condition emits no `Open`/`Close` event because the `if let` only handles `Some -> Some` changes. In that scenario the parent cannot force the current popover state during the first controlled render (for example, closing an uncontrolled picker by setting `open: Some(false)` leaves it open), so compare the newly provided value against the current resolved state or otherwise handle `None -> Some` transitions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "        // Use the unwrapped hue so the thumb stays at the 360° endpoint instead\n        // of collapsing to 0° (ColorValue wraps hue into `[0, 360)`).\n        let value = channel_current(self.ctx, channel);\n        let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n\n        let label = match channel {\n            ColorChannel::Alpha => (self.ctx.messages.alpha_label)(&self.ctx.locale),\n            _ => (self.ctx.messages.hue_label)(&self.ctx.locale),\n        };\n\n        // Alpha lives in `0..=1`, so report `aria-valuenow`/min/max as a 0–100\n        // percentage — `{:.0}` on the raw fraction would round every partial\n        // alpha to 0 or 1 and mislead screen readers. Hue stays in whole degrees.\n        let (value_now, value_min, value_max) = if channel == ColorChannel::Alpha {\n            (value * 100.0, 0.0, 100.0)\n        } else {\n            (value, min, max)\n        };\n\n        attrs\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label)\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueNow), format!(\"{value_now:.0}\"))\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMin), format!(\"{value_min:.0}\"))\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMax), format!(\"{value_max:.0}\"))\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Orientation), \"horizontal\");"

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GM5Pc  file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1075  comments=2
  [chatgpt-codex-connector] **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync open when switching to controlled mode**

When a picker has been mounted uncontrolled (`old.open == None`) and the parent later starts controlling it with `open: Some(false)` or `Some(true)`, this condition emits no `Open`/`Close` event because the `if let` only handles `Some -> Some` changes. In that scenario the parent cannot force the current popover state during the first controlled render (for example, closing an uncontrolled picker by setting `open: Some(false)` leaves it open), so compare the newly provided value against the current resolved state or otherwise handle `None -> Some` transitions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
---
  [fogodev] @codex I believe this is already handled — could you re-check? The guard is `if let (was, Some(now)) = (old.open, new.open) && was != Some(now)`. `was` binds the whole `old.open: Option<bool>`, so for None->Some it evaluates `None != Some(now)`, which is `true` for both `Some(false)` and `Some(true)`. So a None->Some transition DOES push `Open`/`Close`. Added a regression test in 5b770ad2 (`controlled_open_none_to_some_forces_state`) that mounts an uncontrolled picker, opens it, then `set_props(open: Some(false))` and asserts it closes (and the reverse). It passes. Am I missing a scenario where prop-vs-prop diverges from prop-vs-state here? Leaving this thread open for your reply.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GNNw8  file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:840  comments=1
  [chatgpt-codex-connector] **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep controlled open state from drifting**

When `Props::open` is controlled and currently `Some(true)`, `Api::on_trigger_click` dispatches `Toggle`, which reaches this arm and applies `close_plan()` immediately. Because `on_props_changed` only emits an open event when the prop value changes, a parent render that keeps `open: Some(true)` won't restore the state, so `aria-expanded` and the content state can contradict the controlled prop; user-initiated close should be recorded/requested rather than mutating state while `props.open.is_some()`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GNNw-  file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:1031  comments=1
  [chatgpt-codex-connector] **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve hue endpoint across controlled value echoes**

When a controlled hue drag lands at the 360° endpoint, `set_channel_value` intentionally caches `ctx.hue_value = 360` while `ColorValue` wraps the stored hue to 0. If the parent echoes the same controlled color back, this unconditional `sync_hue_from_color` resets the cache to 0, so the hue slider jumps from the right endpoint back to the left even though the user's selected endpoint was preserved before the prop round-trip; mirror `ColorSlider` by not re-deriving hue when the controlled value equals the pending value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GNNxE  file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:586  comments=1
  [chatgpt-codex-connector] **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mirror drag coordinates for RTL pickers**

When `Props::dir` is `Rtl`, the picker mirrors keyboard arrows and exposes `dir` so the visual picker is RTL, but this drag path still maps physical `x = 0` to the minimum saturation/hue/alpha. In an RTL color picker, clicking or dragging the left edge of the area or hue/alpha slider therefore selects the opposite end from the rendered control; invert the normalized x before applying the area/channel value when `ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GNNxG  file: crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_picker/mod.rs:648  comments=1
  [chatgpt-codex-connector] **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh cached hue after RGB channel edits**

When the RGB numeric inputs are used (`color_space == Rgb`), `with_channel` rebuilds the color via RGB conversion and can change the hue, but `ctx.hue_value` is only refreshed for direct hue edits. After changing a red/green/blue channel, the hue slider continues to read and position from the stale cached hue even though the area background and value have moved to the newly computed hue; sync `hue_value` from the resulting color for RGB channel updates.

> AGENT

The library convention is clear: popover and dialog both use `open: Option<bool>` + `on_open_change` callback + `Effect::OpenChange` (optimistic flip + notify). ColorPicker is **missing** the `on_open_change` notification entirely — that's the real gap behind both M5Pc and NNw8. So the convention-aligned fix is to add `on_open_change` + `Effect::OpenChange` (mirroring popover/dialog), plus the 3 bounded fixes (hue echo, RTL drag, hue-after-RGB). Let me implement. First, the `Effect::OpenChange` variant.

Both base the new color on the *pending*\n/// value so a controlled drag-in-flight accumulates rather than re-reading the\n/// stale controlled prop.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => set_area(ctx, x, 1.0 - y),\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);",

Both base the new color on the *pending*\n/// value so a controlled drag-in-flight accumulates rather than re-reading the\n/// stale controlled prop.\n///\n/// In RTL the physical x is mirrored (`1 - x`) before mapping, since the visual\n/// picker is flipped horizontally (the left edge is the maximum), matching the\n/// RTL-mirrored keyboard handling and `ColorArea`/`ColorSlider`.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    let x = if ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl {\n        1.0 - x.clamp(0.0, 1.0)\n    } else {\n        x\n    };\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => set_area(ctx, x, 1.0 - y),\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);"

636	fn set_area(ctx: &mut Context, saturation: f64, y: f64) {
637	    let current = *ctx.value.pending();
638	    let saturation = saturation.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
639	    let y = y.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
640	
641	    let next = if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {
642	        let mut color = ColorValue::from_hsb(current.hue, saturation, y);
643	        color.alpha = current.alpha;
644	        color
645	    } else {
646	        let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, saturation);
647	        with_channel(&updated, ColorChannel::Lightness, y)
648	    };
649	
650	    ctx.value.set(next);
651	}
652	
653	/// Set a single channel on the pending color, space-aware so the value the user
654	/// edits matches the active color space:
655	///
656	/// - **Hue** also updates the unwrapped [`Context::hue_value`] so the 360°
657	///   endpoint survives [`ColorValue`]'s `[0, 360)` wrap.
658	/// - **Saturation in HSB** is HSB saturation (set via [`ColorValue::from_hsb`]
659	///   keeping the current brightness), so the numeric S input stays consistent
660	///   with the HSB area; in every other space it is HSL saturation.
661	/// - All other channels go straight through [`with_channel`].

664	
665	    if channel == ColorChannel::Saturation && ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {
666	        let (hue, _, brightness) = base.to_hsb();
667	        let mut next = ColorValue::from_hsb(hue, value, brightness);
668	        next.alpha = base.alpha;
669	        ctx.value.set(next);
670	        return;
671	    }
672	
673	    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&base, channel, value));
674	    if channel == ColorChannel::Hue {
675	        ctx.hue_value = value.clamp(0.0, 360.0);
676	    }
677	}
678	
679	/// Re-derive the cached unwrapped hue from the current color after an external
680	/// full-color set (text input, swatch, eyedropper, controlled-value sync).
681	const fn sync_hue_from_color(ctx: &mut Context) {
682	    ctx.hue_value = ctx.value.pending().hue;
683	}

979	/// Apply an adapter-normalized pointer position to the color value for the given
980	/// drag target. `Area` maps x→saturation `[0, 1]` and y→the area's vertical
981	/// channel `[1, 0]` (brightness in HSB, lightness otherwise); `Channel` maps x

983	/// so a controlled drag-in-flight accumulates.
984	fn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {
985	    match target {

987	        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {
988	            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);
989	            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);

993	}

997	/// otherwise.

1000	    if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {
1001	        let (_, s, v) = color.to_hsb();
1002	        (s, v)
1003	    } else {
1004	        (color.saturation, color.lightness)

1008	/// Write the area coordinates back to the pending color, space-aware so HSB edits
1009	/// set both axes together via `from_hsb` (no HSL-sat/HSB-bright mixing). Hue/alpha
1010	/// preserved.
1011	fn set_area(ctx: &mut Context, saturation: f64, y: f64) {
1012	    let current = *ctx.value.pending();
1013	    let s = saturation.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
1014	    let y = y.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
1015	    let next = if ctx.color_space == ColorSpace::Hsb {
1016	        let mut color = ColorValue::from_hsb(current.hue, s, y);
1017	        color.alpha = current.alpha;
1018	        color
1019	    } else {
1020	        let updated = with_channel(&current, ColorChannel::Saturation, s);
1021	        with_channel(&updated, ColorChannel::Lightness, y)
1022	    };
1023	    ctx.value.set(next);
1024	}

  "new_string": "/// In RTL the physical x is mirrored (`1 - x`) before mapping — the visual picker\n/// is flipped horizontally (left edge = maximum), matching the RTL keyboard\n/// handling and `ColorArea`/`ColorSlider`.\nfn apply_drag_position(ctx: &mut Context, target: DragTarget, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    let x = if ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl { 1.0 - x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) } else { x };\n    match target {\n        DragTarget::Area => set_area(ctx, x, 1.0 - y),\n        DragTarget::Channel(channel) => {\n            let (min, max) = channel_range(channel);\n            let value = min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (max - min);\n            set_channel_value(ctx, channel, value);\n        }\n    }\n}"

> AGENT

Round 6 implemented: 111 tests pass, no orphan snapshots, spec synced. Clippy + coverage gate (`bigaqhxoe`) running. Findings handled:

- **NNw8 + M5Pc (open model):** the real gap was that ColorPicker lacked the `on_open_change` notification popover/dialog have. Added `Props::on_open_change` + `Effect::OpenChange` (fired on every open/close and booted-open), matching the overlay-sibling convention (optimistic flip + notify). M5Pc's specific None→Some claim remains a false positive (proven by test), now also covered by the notification.
- **NNw- (controlled echo):** `SyncValue` no longer re-derives hue when the parent echoes the pending value, preserving the 360° endpoint (mirrors `ColorArea`).
- **NNxE (RTL drag):** `apply_drag_position` mirrors physical x (`1 − x`) in RTL for area + channel drags.
- **NNxG (hue after RGB):** `set_channel_value` refreshes `hue_value` after RGB edits (which recompute hue).

One judgment call to flag: NNw8 literally asks for *strict* controlled semantics (don't mutate state while `open.is_some()`), but popover and dialog both use optimistic-flip-plus-`on_open_change`. I matched that established convention rather than making ColorPicker behave differently from its overlay siblings; strict-controlled would be a library-wide change. I'll note this in the thread reply. Once the gate is green I'll commit/push, reply+resolve the threads, and re-trigger Codex.
